definition_zh: 宽容；容忍；忍耐力；公差；耐受力
definition_en: the willingness to accept behaviour or opinions different from your own, or the ability to endure something difficult without harm
core_image: 一个人把重物扛在肩上，压得弯了腰却没有把重物扔下去
scene: 师傅带着徒弟在车床边量一个轴，卡尺读数总比图纸大上一丝。The machinist explained that a little tolerance is built into every part so that it will still fit.
sceneCN: 这里 tolerance 是机械加工中的「公差」（第 4 个义项：允许的尺寸偏差）；句意为师傅解释说每个零件都留了一点公差，这样才装得进去。画面里有车床、卡尺与图纸。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去掉后缀 -ance 构成动词，义为「容忍；忍受」
由动词加 -ant 构成形容词，义为「宽容的；能耐受的」
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「宽容地」
加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「不宽容；不耐受」

senses.title: Willingness to accept differences
senses.definition: the quality of accepting opinions, beliefs, or customs that differ from one's own
senses.definitionCN: 接受与自己不同的观点、信仰或习俗的品质
senses.example: His tolerance of other faiths made him welcome in every village.
senses.exampleCN: 他对其他信仰的宽容使他在每个村子都受到欢迎。
senses.why: The word comes from a Latin verb meaning to bear or endure, and accepting difference is a way of bearing what is not ours.
senses.whyCN: 本词来自拉丁语中表示「承担、忍受」的动词，接受差异就是承担不属于自己的东西。

senses.title: The capacity to endure hardship
senses.definition: the ability to put up with pain, noise, or difficulty without breaking down
senses.definitionCN: 承受痛苦、噪音或困难而不垮掉的能力
senses.example: Years of field work had raised his tolerance for cold and hunger.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的野外工作提高了他对寒冷和饥饿的忍耐力。
senses.why: Bearing a load physically becomes bearing hardship mentally, so the same noun covers both.
senses.whyCN: 身体上承担重量，自然转为精神上承担艰苦，同一个名词就兼指两者。

senses.title: Biological resistance to a substance
senses.definition: the body's ability to take a drug, poison, or food without harmful effects
senses.definitionCN: 身体服用药物、毒物或食物而不受伤害的能力
senses.example: Long use of the medicine can build up a tolerance, so the dose must be raised.
senses.exampleCN: 长期服用这种药会产生耐受性，因此剂量必须加大。
senses.why: A body that bears a substance without harm is literally enduring it, which is the oldest sense of the root.
senses.whyCN: 身体能承受某种物质而不受伤害，正是词根最古老意义上的「忍受」。

senses.title: Allowed variation in engineering
senses.definition: the amount by which a measurement may vary and still be acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 测量值允许变动而仍属合格的范围
senses.example: Each bolt is cut within a tolerance of a tenth of a millimetre.
senses.exampleCN: 每颗螺栓的切割都控制在十分之一毫米的公差内。
senses.why: A workshop bears a small error the way a person bears an annoyance, and this mechanical sense grew in the machine age.
senses.whyCN: 车间容忍一点误差，正如人容忍一点冒犯，这个机械义项是在机器时代长出来的。

senses.title: Open-mindedness in public life
senses.definition: a social attitude that lets unpopular views be expressed without punishment
senses.definitionCN: 允许不受欢迎的观点被表达而不受惩罚的社会态度
senses.example: The reform was praised as a step towards greater religious tolerance in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革被誉为该地区走向更大的宗教宽容的一步。
senses.why: When the capacity to bear extends beyond one person to a whole society, it becomes a public principle.
senses.whyCN: 当这种承受能力从一个人扩展到整个社会，它就成了公共原则。

senses.title: The margin allowed in a plan
senses.definition: a margin left in a budget, schedule, or system so that small problems do not ruin it
senses.definitionCN: 预算、进度或系统中预留的余地，使小问题不会毁掉全局
senses.example: We left a week of tolerance in the schedule for bad weather.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在日程里留了一周的余量以应对坏天气。
senses.why: A tolerance is always a space that can absorb a knock, whether in metal or in a timetable.
senses.whyCN: 公差永远是能吸收撞击的一块空间，无论它出现在金属里还是日程里。

senses.title: Refusal to forbid what one dislikes
senses.definition: the practice of allowing something one disapproves of rather than banning it
senses.definitionCN: 对自己不赞成的事不加禁止的做法
senses.example: Her tolerance of noisy neighbours did not mean she liked the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 她对吵闹邻居的容忍并不意味着她喜欢那种噪音。
senses.why: This sense stresses the negative side of bearing: not approving, merely not stopping.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项强调「承受」的否定面：并不赞同，只是没有制止。

senses.title: The limit of what can be borne
senses.definition: the point at which patience or endurance finally gives way
senses.definitionCN: 耐心或耐力最终崩溃的那一刻
senses.example: The crowd's tolerance broke when the third train was cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 第三趟列车被取消时，人群的忍耐到了极限。
senses.why: Every tolerance has an edge, and naming the edge turns the noun into a measure of the breaking point.
senses.whyCN: 任何容忍都有边界，把边界说出来，这个名词就成了崩溃点的度量。

intro.en: The word goes back through French to Latin tolerare, to bear or put up with, a verb whose exact prehistory is debated but whose sense has stayed remarkably steady for two thousand years.
intro.cn: 本词经法语上溯到拉丁语 tolerare（承担、忍受），这个词动词的更深来源尚有争议，但其含义两千年来相当稳定。

items.en: Tolerare means to bear, endure, or put up with, and is used of carrying a load as well as of enduring a person.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tolerare 意为「承担、忍受」，既用于扛负重物，也用于忍受某个人。

items.en: The related adjective tolerabilis describes what can be borne, and the noun tolerantia names the bearing itself.
items.cn: 相关形容词 tolerabilis 表示「可以承受的」，名词 tolerantia 则指承受这件事本身。

items.en: Old French tolerance keeps the medical and moral senses of the Latin noun in the learned register.
items.cn: 古法语 tolerance 在书面语中保留了拉丁名词的医学与道德含义。

items.en: English borrows the word in the sixteenth century, first for the bearing of pain and then for the bearing of differences of creed.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入此词，先指忍受疼痛，继而指容忍教义上的差异。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the political sense of letting dissenting churches exist is well established.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，「允许异议教派存在」的政治含义已经完全确立。

items.en: Engineering takes the word up in the nineteenth century for the permitted error in a measurement, and the biological sense of drug tolerance follows in the twentieth.
items.cn: 工程学在十九世纪用它表示测量中允许的误差，二十世纪又出现药物耐受性这一生物学含义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same Latin stem, while the near-meaning group gathers terms for patience and for limits set in numbers.
note.cn: 形近组收集建立在同一拉丁词干上的词，近义组则汇集表示耐心以及用数字设定的限度的词。

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the Latin stem, from the common collocations, and from the word family built with -ant and -ate.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从拉丁词干、常用搭配以及用 -ant 和 -ate 构成的词族入手。

normal.en: Tolerare meant to carry a weight, so tolerance is a muscle that has learned to carry.
normal.cn: tolerare 意为扛重量，所以 tolerance 是一块学会负重的肌肉。

normal.en: Tolerate is the verb, tolerant the adjective, tolerance the noun: -ate, -ant, -ance.
normal.cn: tolerate 是动词，tolerant 是形容词，tolerance 是名词，后缀依次为 -ate、-ant、-ance。

normal.en: Zero tolerance is a policy phrase, and the zero shows that the limit has been set at nothing.
normal.cn: zero tolerance 是政策用语，那个零说明限度被设为零。

normal.en: In a workshop, tolerance is the small space that lets a metal part slide in instead of jamming.
normal.cn: 在车间里，公差是让金属件能滑进去而不是卡住的那点缝隙。

normal.en: Drug tolerance means the body has learned to carry the dose, so the dose must grow.
normal.cn: 药物耐受性指身体学会了扛住这个剂量，于是剂量必须增加。

abstract.en: Picture a porter with a crate on his back who does not set it down at the first step.
abstract.cn: 想象一名脚夫背着木箱，走第一步时并没有把它放下。

abstract.en: Think of a door frame made a millimetre too wide, and the door that never sticks.
abstract.cn: 想一个做宽了一毫米的门框，和一扇从此不再卡住的门。

abstract.en: Tolerance is a deliberately loose grip: tight enough to hold, loose enough to let air through.
abstract.cn: 容忍是一种故意放松的握法：紧到能握住，松到能让空气通过。

examples.en: The school teaches tolerance of different backgrounds.
examples.cn: 这所学校教导学生宽容不同的背景。

examples.en: Repeated use of the painkiller raised her tolerance to it.
examples.cn: 反复使用这种止痛药提高了她对它的耐受性。

examples.en: The parts are machined to a tolerance of one hundredth of a millimetre.
examples.cn: 这些零件被加工到百分之一毫米的公差。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「托了忍死」——托着、忍着，忍到死也不松手，就是容忍。

root: 拉丁语 tolerare（承担、忍受）→ tolerantia（忍受）→ 古法语 tolerance → 英语 tolerance。同族词有 tolerate、tolerant、tolerable；词根更深层的来源，一般认为与「举起、支撑」一类词形有关，但尚无定论。

sensesIntro.en: From the single image of bearing a load, the entry spreads outwards: bearing other people, bearing pain, bearing a drug, and finally the measured margin that lets metal or schedules absorb a knock.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「承受重量」这一个意象出发，本词向外展开：承受他人、承受痛苦、承受药物，最后是让金属或日程吸收撞击的那段可量度的余量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a load carried on the shoulders without dropping it.
core.cn: 核心意象：肩上的重物被一直扛着，没有放下。

branches.en: Bearing other people and their differences.
branches.cn: 承受他人及其差异。

branches.en: Bearing hardship, and the moment the bearing fails.
branches.cn: 承受艰苦，以及承受失灵的那一刻。

branches.en: Bearing a substance inside the body.
branches.cn: 身体内部承受某种物质。

branches.en: Bearing a measured error in a machine.
branches.cn: 承受机器上可量度的误差。

branches.en: Bearing a knock in time, money, or plans.
branches.cn: 在时间、金钱或计划中承受意外撞击。

intro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb stem with the noun ending -ance, and its family is formed with -ate, -ant, -able, and the negative prefix in-.
intro.cn: 本词由拉丁动词词干加名词后缀 -ance 构成，同族词由 -ate、-ant、-able 与否定前缀 in- 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries below show the verb and adjectives from which the English family descends.
latinIntro.cn: 下面列出的拉丁词条是英语这一词族所由来的动词与形容词。

items.example: The stem carries the whole word family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干撑起整个词族。

items.example: Tolerance is the state of bearing.

items.meaning: the same suffix in its French shape
items.example: Both spellings appear in learned borrowings.
items.exampleCN: 两种拼法都出现在借入的书面词里。

items.example: Tolerate is the verb.

items.meaning: one who or that which does
items.example: Tolerant describes the person who bears.
Tolerable means it can be borne.
Intolerance is the lack of tolerance.
Tolerantly adds the adverb ending.

items.meaning: a system of belief or practice
items.example: The pattern appears in other social nouns.
items.exampleCN: 这一构词模式也出现在其他社会名词中。

latinEntries.meaning: to bear, endure, put up with

definition_zh: 容忍；忍受；容许；对……有耐受力
definition_en: to allow something you dislike to happen or exist without protest, or to endure something painful or unpleasant
core_image: 双手按住桌沿，任由对面的人大声说话，始终没有起身离开
scene: 会议室里有人把空调开得很低，靠窗的同事只把外套披上，一言不发。She can tolerate the cold office far better than a heated argument.
sceneCN: 这里 tolerate 是「忍受」（第 2 个义项：忍受不适）；句意为她对寒冷的办公室的忍受力远胜于对一场激烈争吵的忍受力。画面里有冷气口、外套与沉默的同事。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ance 构成名词，义为「宽容；忍耐力；公差」
由动词加 -ant 构成形容词，义为「宽容的」
由动词加 -able 构成，义为「可忍受的；尚可的」
由动词加 -ation 构成，义为「容许；信仰宽容」

senses.title: To allow what one dislikes
senses.definition: to let something happen or exist although one disapproves of it
senses.definitionCN: 虽然不赞成，仍让某事发生或存在
senses.example: The teacher will not tolerate cheating in any form.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老师不容忍任何形式的作弊。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to bear, and letting an unwanted thing stay is the everyday shape of bearing it.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为承担，让不想要的东西留在身边，就是「承担」的日常形态。

senses.title: To endure discomfort
senses.definition: to put up with pain, heat, noise, or another unpleasant condition
senses.definitionCN: 忍受疼痛、高温、噪音或其他不适条件
senses.example: Few plants can tolerate this salt-laden soil.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有植物能忍受这种含盐的土壤。
senses.why: The physical sense of carrying a burden is still visible here: the body holds the discomfort without giving way.
senses.whyCN: 背负重物的身体感在这里仍然可见：身体撑住不适而不垮。

senses.title: To bear a person
senses.definition: to accept a difficult person without breaking the relationship
senses.definitionCN: 接受一个难相处的人而不把关系弄僵
senses.example: He tolerated his uncle's teasing throughout the whole dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 整顿晚饭他都容忍着叔叔的取笑。
senses.why: Bearing a weight and bearing a person are the same effort of self-control in Latin idiom.
senses.whyCN: 在拉丁语习惯里，承担重量与承担一个人是同一份自制的力。

senses.title: To accept a substance safely
senses.definition: of the body, to take a drug or food without harm
senses.definitionCN: 指身体能服用药物或食物而不受伤害
senses.example: Some patients cannot tolerate penicillin and need another drug.
senses.exampleCN: 有些病人不能耐受青霉素，需要换一种药。
senses.why: A body that lets a substance remain inside without damage is bearing it in the strictest sense.
senses.whyCN: 身体让某种物质留在体内而不受损，正是最严格意义上的承受。

senses.title: To permit by law or custom
senses.definition: to permit an activity officially or by long custom
senses.definitionCN: 在法律或长期习俗上准许某项活动
senses.example: The old city tolerates street musicians in the square until midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老城容许街头乐手在广场演奏到午夜。
senses.why: When the bearing hand is a whole community, tolerating becomes a licence rather than a feeling.
senses.whyCN: 当承受者是整个共同体，容忍就由心情变成了许可。

senses.title: To survive under difficult conditions
senses.definition: of a plant or animal, to survive and grow in a harsh environment
senses.definitionCN: 指动植物在恶劣环境中存活生长
senses.example: These shrubs tolerate drought and poor soil better than any grass.
senses.exampleCN: 这些灌木比任何草类都更能耐受干旱与贫瘠的土壤。
senses.why: Surviving a hard environment is bearing it for a lifetime, so the word moves from feeling to biology.
senses.whyCN: 在严酷环境中活下来，就是把环境承受一辈子，于是这个词从感受走向生物。

senses.title: To accept without correcting
senses.definition: to let an error or fault pass unnoticed or uncorrected
senses.definitionCN: 让错误或过失被忽视、不加纠正
senses.example: The editor tolerated a few awkward lines in an otherwise strong report.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑默许了这篇总体有力的报告里几处生硬的句子。
senses.why: Here the bearing is quiet: nothing is approved, but nothing is stopped either.
senses.whyCN: 这里的承受是无声的：既没有认可，也没有阻止。

senses.title: To hold evidence without rejecting it
senses.definition: in measurement, to allow results to fall within an accepted range
senses.definitionCN: 在测量中允许结果落在可接受的范围内
senses.example: The instrument can tolerate a drift of two degrees before a reading is discarded.
senses.exampleCN: 仪器能容许两度的漂移，超出才作废读数。
senses.why: The engineering notion of a permissible margin is the technical child of the old verb for bearing.
senses.whyCN: 工程上「允许的范围」这一概念，就是「承受」这个老动词的现代技术后代。

intro.en: Tolerate is the English verb formed on Latin tolerare, to bear; the deeper origin of the Latin word is uncertain and competing explanations have been offered.
intro.cn: tolerate 是在拉丁语 tolerare（承担、忍受）基础上形成的英语动词；这个词的更深来源不确定，学界有几种互相竞争的解释。

items.en: Tolerare means to bear up under a burden, and Roman writers use it for enduring pain, work, and difficult people.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tolerare 意为在重负下撑住，罗马作家用它表示忍受疼痛、劳苦与难缠的人。

items.en: The past participle toleratus and the adjective tolerabilis are common in classical prose.
items.cn: 过去分词 toleratus 与形容词 tolerabilis 在古典散文中很常见。

items.en: The link to ferre, to carry, is sometimes proposed, but the etymology is generally marked as uncertain.
items.cn: 有人提出它与表示「携带」的 ferre 有关，但词源一般被标为不确定。

items.en: English forms tolerate in the sixteenth century, first in the physical sense and soon in the moral one.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪构成 tolerate，先用于身体方面，很快扩展到道德方面。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the verb is used of religious and political forbearance.
items.cn: 十七世纪起，这个动词用于宗教与政治上的宽容。

items.en: In the nineteenth century medicine and engineering give the word its senses of drug tolerance and permitted error.
items.cn: 十九世纪，医学与工程学赋予它药物耐受与允许误差的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the noun and adjective of the same family, while the near-meaning group places the verb among words for putting up with and for allowing.
note.cn: 形近组收集同一词族的名词与形容词，近义组则把这个动词放进「忍受」与「容许」的语义场。

normalIntro.en: These memories build on the Latin verb, on the suffixes, and on the way the word moves from feelings to machines.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从拉丁动词、后缀构词以及这个词由感受走向机器的路径入手。

normal.en: Tolerare is to carry, so to tolerate is to carry something you would rather put down.
normal.cn: tolerare 是扛，所以 tolerate 就是扛着一件你更想放下的东西。

normal.en: Tolerance, tolerant, tolerable all share the stem; only the endings change the part of speech.
normal.cn: tolerance、tolerant、tolerable 共用一个词干，只是词尾改变了词性。

normal.en: Cannot tolerate is the standard negative, and the modal shows that bearing has a limit.
normal.cn: cannot tolerate 是标准否定式，情态动词说明承受是有上限的。

normal.en: Plants that tolerate salt are said to be salt-tolerant, a compound made from the adjective.
normal.cn: 耐盐的植物被称为 salt-tolerant，这个词是用形容词构成的复合词。

normal.en: In a lab, an instrument tolerates drift, which links the verb to the idea of a permitted margin.
normal.cn: 在实验室里，仪器容忍漂移，这把这个动词和「允许的余量」联系起来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a hot cup that stays there one more second than it wants to.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手握着烫杯，比它想握的时间多坚持了一秒。

abstract.en: Think of a bridge that bends a little in the wind instead of breaking, and that bending is tolerance.
abstract.cn: 想一座在风里略微弯曲而不折断的桥，那一点弯曲就是承受。

abstract.en: To tolerate is to leave the door unlocked for a guest you do not entirely trust.
abstract.cn: 容忍就是给一个你并不完全信任的客人留一扇没锁的门。

examples.en: We do not tolerate bullying in this club.
examples.cn: 在这个社团里我们不容忍欺凌。

examples.en: The workers tolerated the heat until the fans were repaired.
examples.cn: 工人们一直忍受着高温，直到风扇被修好。

examples.en: Certain grasses tolerate salt water better than others.
examples.cn: 有些草类比其他草类更能耐受咸水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「托了忍特」——托着、忍着，还特别能忍，就是容忍、忍受。

root: 拉丁语 tolerare（承担、忍受），同族名词 tolerantia、形容词 tolerabilis。词根更深来源不确定，一般认为与表示「举起、支撑」一类词形有关，但无定论。

sensesIntro.en: The entry runs from allowing an unwelcome act through enduring discomfort, bearing a difficult person, surviving a substance or a climate, and finally tolerating error in law and in instruments.
sensesIntro.cn: 本词从容许不受欢迎的行为，经忍受不适、容忍难缠的人、耐受某种物质或气候，最后到法律与仪器上容许误差。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: carrying a weight and choosing not to drop it.
core.cn: 核心意象：扛着重量，选择不放下。

branches.en: Allowing what one dislikes to continue.
branches.cn: 让不喜欢的继续存在。

branches.en: Bearing discomfort and difficult people.
branches.cn: 忍受不适与难相处的人。

branches.en: Bearing a substance in the body.
branches.cn: 身体承受某种物质。

branches.en: Allowing by law or custom.
branches.cn: 在法律或习俗上准许。

branches.en: Surviving a hard environment or a measured margin.
branches.cn: 在严酷环境或可量度的误差中存活。

intro.en: The verb is a Latin stem with the verb ending -ate, and the family is completed with -ance, -ant, -able, and -ation.
intro.cn: 这个动词是拉丁词干加动词词尾 -ate，同族词由 -ance、-ant、-able 与 -ation 补全。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the verb and its near relatives that English borrowed or refashioned.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁词条给出英语借入或改形的动词及其近亲。

items.example: The stem is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干是整个词族的基础。

items.example: Tolerate is built with this ending.
Tolerance names the state.
Tolerant describes the attitude.
Tolerable means bearable.
Toleration is the older noun for the practice.
items.exampleCN: toleration 是表示这种做法的老名词。

items.example: Intolerant adds the negative.
Tolerantly is the adverb.
Tolerating opens a modifying phrase.
items.exampleCN: tolerating 可以引导修饰短语。

definition_zh: 西红柿；番茄；番茄果实
definition_en: a soft round red fruit with many small seeds, eaten raw in salads or cooked in sauces
core_image: 藤上挂着几颗果皮紧绷的红果，用手一掐就渗出汁水
scene: 夏天傍晚，菜园的木架上爬满了藤，有几颗果实红得发亮。She picked a ripe tomato and ate it warm from the sun.
sceneCN: 这里 tomato 就是「西红柿」这一果实（第 1 个义项：藤上的番茄果实）；句意为她摘下一颗熟透的西红柿，趁还被太阳晒得温热时吃掉了。画面里有菜园木架、藤蔓与红果。

pos.zh: 名词：西红柿；西红柿果实
名词：西红柿植株（园艺用法）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加复数词尾 -es 构成，义为「西红柿（复数）」
口语中加 -ey 构成，义为「带着番茄味与番茄气的」
复合名词，义为「番茄膏；浓缩番茄酱」

senses.title: The red fruit on the vine
senses.definition: the soft red fruit of a plant of the nightshade family, eaten as a vegetable
senses.definitionCN: 茄科植物的柔软红色果实，被当作蔬菜食用
senses.example: She sliced a warm tomato straight from the garden onto the bread.
senses.exampleCN: 她把刚从园里摘下的温热西红柿切成片放在面包上。
senses.why: The word names the plant before it names the fruit, exactly as it did when it arrived from the Americas.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先指植株再指果实，与它从美洲传入时的情况一致。

senses.title: The plant that bears the fruit
senses.definition: the bushy plant with hairy stems and yellow flowers that produces tomatoes
senses.definitionCN: 茎上有毛、开黄花、结番茄的灌木状植物
senses.example: The tomatoes along the south wall need staking before the wind rises.
senses.exampleCN: 南墙边的西红柿需要在大风来前绑上支架。
senses.why: Since one plant can carry many fruits, the plural form often names the plants in a garden.
senses.whyCN: 一株能结很多果，所以复数常指园子里的植株。

senses.title: The fruit in cooking
senses.definition: the fruit as an ingredient, used for sauce, soup, or juice
senses.definitionCN: 作为食材的番茄，用于酱汁、汤或果汁
senses.example: Long cooking turns the tomato sweet and thickens the sauce.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间炖煮会让番茄变甜，酱汁也随之变稠。
senses.why: Once processed, the fruit stops being a thing on a plate and becomes a flavour base.
senses.whyCN: 一旦被加工，这颗果就不再是盘中之物，而成了味道的底子。

senses.title: The colour of the fruit
senses.definition: a strong red colour like that of a ripe tomato
senses.definitionCN: 像熟透西红柿那样浓烈的红色
senses.example: The kitchen wall was painted tomato, which made the small room glow.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房墙刷成番茄红，让小房间显得发亮。
senses.why: Bright fruits often give their names to colours, and this one is now a standard paint chip.
senses.whyCN: 鲜艳的果实常把自己的名字借给颜色，如今它已是一个标准的漆色名。

senses.title: The word as a term in biology
senses.definition: in botany, Solanum lycopersicum, whose fruit is classed as a berry
senses.definitionCN: 植物学中指 Solanum lycopersicum，其果实属于浆果
senses.example: Botanists class the tomato as a berry, though cooks treat it as a vegetable.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学家把番茄归为浆果，尽管厨师把它当蔬菜。
senses.why: The fruit develops from a single ovary with soft flesh, which is the botanical test for a berry.
senses.whyCN: 这种果由单个子房发育、果肉柔软，正好符合植物学上「浆果」的判断标准。

senses.title: The American pronunciation split
senses.definition: the vowel of the second syllable differs between British and American speech
senses.definitionCN: 第二音节元音在英式与美式发音中不同
senses.example: Visitors from different countries argue about how the tomato should be said.
senses.exampleCN: 来自不同国家的访客会为这个词该怎么读争论。
senses.why: The word travelled into English twice, and the two vowel shapes survive as accents.
senses.whyCN: 这个词两次进入英语，两种元音形态就以口音的形式留了下来。

senses.title: The tomato as a cultural symbol
senses.definition: the fruit as an emblem of long life in some cultures, or of the summer table in others
senses.definitionCN: 在某些文化里象征长寿，在另一些文化里象征夏日餐桌的果实
senses.example: On the painted bowl, a single tomato promises a long and full life.
senses.exampleCN: 在那只彩绘碗上，一颗番茄寓意长寿与丰足。
senses.why: Round red fruits appear in folk decoration where abundance is wished, so the fruit carries meaning beyond food.
senses.whyCN: 圆而红的果实在民间图案里用来祈求丰足，于是它承载了食物之外的意义。

senses.title: The tomato as a household staple
senses.definition: the fruit regarded as an ordinary item of the weekly shopping
senses.definitionCN: 被视为每周采购清单里最普通一员的番茄
senses.example: A bowl of tomatoes sat on the counter beside the bread and the salt.
senses.exampleCN: 一只盛着番茄的碗放在台面上，旁边是面包和盐。
senses.why: As soon as a food is cheap enough to buy weekly, its name becomes an ordinary household word.
senses.whyCN: 当一种食物便宜到可以每周买，它的名字就成了寻常家常用语。

intro.en: The word reached Europe through Spanish from Nahuatl tomatl, the language of central Mexico, and the botanical name added by Linnaeus keeps that origin.
intro.cn: 这个词经西班牙语从墨西哥中部的纳瓦特尔语 tomatl 传入欧洲，林奈所定的学名保留了这个来源。

items.en: The Spanish settlers first used the word for a related green fruit, and early Italian writers called it pomo d'oro, the golden apple.
items.cn: 西班牙殖民者最初用这个词指一种相近的绿色果实，早期意大利作家把它称为 pomo d'oro，即金苹果。

items.en: French travellers borrowed the fruit under Italian names before the Spanish word came north.
items.cn: 法国旅行者先以意大利名称借入这种果实，西班牙语的词形后来才北上。

items.en: English adopts tomato in the seventeenth century, soon after the plant arrives in European gardens.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 tomato，此时这种植物刚进入欧洲花园不久。

items.en: For two centuries the fruit is treated with suspicion by English cooks, who grow it mainly for medicine and ornament.
items.cn: 有两个世纪，英国的厨师对这种果实心存疑虑，主要种来入药与观赏。

items.en: By the nineteenth century tomato sauce and canned tomato make the word an everyday item of the kitchen.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，番茄酱与罐装番茄让这个词成了厨房里的日常用语。

items.en: Linnaeus had already placed the plant in Solanum, and the species name lycopersicum means wolf peach.
items.cn: 林奈早已把这种植物归入茄属，种名 lycopersicum 意为「狼桃」。

note.en: The look-alike group collects other names of the same nightshade family, while the near-meaning group gathers kitchen words that describe the fruit and its uses.
note.cn: 形近组收集同属茄科的其他名物，近义组则汇集描述这种果实及其用法的厨房词汇。

entries.definition: a starchy root vegetable of the same family
entries.definitionCN: 土豆；马铃薯，与番茄同属茄科，只是拼写相近

entries.definition: the plural of the fruit
a small green fruit used in Mexican sauces
entries.definitionCN: 墨西哥青番茄，同源词形

entries.definition: a bicycle for two riders, one behind the other
entries.definitionCN: 双人自行车，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the seed-bearing part of a plant used as food
a plant or plant part eaten with savoury dishes
the red pigment that gives the fruit its colour
a strong-flavoured bulb used as a base in cooking

normalIntro.en: These memories use the Nahuatl origin, the plural spelling, the compound kitchen phrases, and the British and American vowels.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用纳瓦特尔语来源、复数拼法、厨房复合词以及英美元音差异。

normal.en: The Nahuatl word was tomatl, and the Spanish added a vowel while keeping the stem.
normal.cn: 纳瓦特尔语原词是 tomatl，西班牙语保留了词干并加上了元音。

normal.en: The plural is tomatoes with -es, not tomatos, just as potato makes potatoes.
normal.cn: 复数是 tomatoes，用 -es 而非 -os，和 potato 变 potatoes 一样。

normal.en: Tomato sauce, tomato juice, and tomato soup show the fruit as an ingredient.
normal.cn: tomato sauce、tomato juice、tomato soup 表明这种果可以当食材。

normal.en: Cherry tomato names the small salad variety, and the modifier tells the size.
normal.cn: cherry tomato 指做沙拉的小品种，前面的修饰语说明大小。

normal.en: Britons say a long ah in the middle and Americans a long ay, and both are correct.
normal.cn: 英国人把中间读成长音 ah，美国人读成长音 ay，两种都对。

abstract.en: Picture a warm red globe that splits at the press of a thumb and leaves your hand smelling of green vine.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗温热的红色小球，拇指一按就裂开，手上留下藤叶的青气。

abstract.en: Think of a bottle of sauce tipped over a plate of pasta, and the red slowly covering the white.
abstract.cn: 想一瓶酱汁倒在盘中的意面上，红色慢慢盖过白色。

abstract.en: The word itself travelled from Mexico to Spain to Italy to England, and the fruit followed the same road.
abstract.cn: 这个词从墨西哥到西班牙、到意大利、到英格兰，果实也走了同一条路。

examples.en: She grows tomatoes and herbs on the balcony.
examples.cn: 她在阳台上种番茄和香草。

examples.en: Add a sliced tomato to the salad just before serving.
examples.cn: 上菜前再加一个切片西红柿到沙拉里。

examples.en: The recipe calls for two tomatoes and a spoonful of paste.
examples.cn: 这道菜谱要两个西红柿和一勺番茄膏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特玛托」——特玛托着一筐红果去集市上卖，就是番茄。

root: 纳瓦特尔语 tomatl → 西班牙语 tomate → 英语 tomato。学名 Solanum lycopersicum 由林奈确定，种名意为「狼桃」。与 potato 只是同属茄科、拼写相近，并非同一词根。

sensesIntro.en: The entry starts from the fruit on the vine and moves to the plant itself, the fruit as an ingredient, its colour, its botanical status, its pronunciation, and finally its everyday and symbolic life.
sensesIntro.cn: 本词条目从藤上的果实写起，再转到植株本身、作为食材的果、它的颜色、植物学身份、读音，最后是它在日常生活与象征里的位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tight red globe hanging from a green vine.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗紧实的红果挂在绿色藤蔓上。

branches.en: The fruit and the plant that bears it.
branches.cn: 果实与结出果实的植株。

branches.en: The fruit as food and as a weekly purchase.
branches.cn: 作为食物与每周采购品的果。

branches.en: The colour borrowed from the fruit.
branches.cn: 从果实借来的颜色。

branches.en: The fruit as a botanical category.
branches.cn: 作为植物学分类的果。

branches.en: The word in speech and in symbol.
branches.cn: 这个词在口音与象征中的形态。

intro.en: The word is a borrowed Nahuatl root reshaped by Spanish, so English affixes are mostly plural and compound endings.
intro.cn: 本词是经西班牙语改形的纳瓦特尔语词根，英语里能加的构词成分主要是复数词尾与复合形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries here are the scientific names attached to the plant, not ancestors of the everyday word.
latinIntro.cn: 这里的拉丁词条是附加于该植物的学名成分，而不是日常用词的祖先。

items.meaning: the fruit of the tomato plant
items.example: The stem is unchanged in English.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干在英语中没有变化。

items.meaning: ending added when the word was borrowed
items.meaningCN: 借入时添加的收尾元音
items.example: Spanish tomate and English tomato differ only here.
items.exampleCN: 西班牙语 tomate 与英语 tomato 只在这里不同。

items.meaning: used after a consonant plus o
items.meaningCN: 辅音加 o 之后的复数词尾
items.example: Tomatoes follows the same pattern as potatoes.
items.exampleCN: tomatoes 与 potatoes 属同一模式。

items.meaningCN: 小的、圆形的、做沙拉用的
items.example: Cherry tomato names a small variety.
items.exampleCN: cherry tomato 指一种小品种。

items.meaning: a thick liquid served with food
items.meaningCN: 浇在食物上的浓稠汁液
items.example: Tomato sauce is the everyday compound.
items.exampleCN: tomato sauce 是最常用的复合词。

items.example: Tomato paste is reduced fruit.
items.exampleCN: tomato paste 是收浓的果浆。

items.example: Tomato juice is served cold.

items.structure: Greek combining form in the species name
items.example: Lycopersicum uses this element in the botanical name.
items.exampleCN: Lycopersicum 在学名中用到这个成分。

items.structure: Latin element in the species name

definition_zh: 明天；明日；未来；将来
definition_en: the day after today, or the near future that has not come yet
core_image: 窗外的天色还没亮，桌上放着一张写着明日的车票
scene: 深夜的教室里，最后一盏灯也要熄了，值日生把黑板擦干净才走。The exam is tomorrow morning, so everyone went to bed early.
sceneCN: 这里 tomorrow 是「明天」这一天（第 1 个义项：今天的下一天）；句意为考试就在明天上午，于是大家都早早上床。画面里有熄灯的教室、擦净的黑板与走廊。

derivatives.zh: 由名词加复数词尾 -s 构成，义为「一个又一个明天」
由同一构词模式 todæg 演化而来，义为「今天」
由同一构词模式构成的同族词，义为「今晚」

senses.title: The day after today
senses.definition: the day that follows the present day
senses.definitionCN: 紧接在今天之后的那一天
senses.example: We will finish the report tomorrow, before the office opens.
senses.exampleCN: 我们明天在办公室开门前把报告写完。
senses.why: The Old English form joins the word for morrow with the preposition to, so the word literally points at the next day.
senses.whyCN: 古英语形式把表示「次日」的词与介词 to 连在一起，字面上就是「指向下一天」。

senses.title: The near future
senses.definition: the time that is still to come, especially the near future
senses.definitionCN: 尚未到来的时间，尤指不久之后
senses.example: The engineers spoke of the city of tomorrow as if they could already walk in it.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师们谈起未来的城市，仿佛已经能在其中行走。
senses.why: One step beyond the next morning, the word becomes a name for any time not yet reached.
senses.whyCN: 再往前一步，这个词就成了任何尚未抵达之时间的名字。

senses.title: Morning as a time of day
senses.definition: in older usage, the morning hours of any day
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，任何一天的早晨时段
senses.example: Good morrow to you, the old greeting said, wishing a fine morning.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的问候语会说 good morrow，祝愿对方有个美好的早晨。
senses.why: The morrow of the word is the same morrow that meant morning, and that older sense survives in greetings.
senses.whyCN: 词中的 morrow 就是表示「早晨」的那个 morrow，这个古义在问候语里留了下来。

senses.title: A promise about the future
senses.definition: a pledge that something will be done on the next day or later
senses.definitionCN: 保证在某天或之后去做某事的承诺
senses.example: He kept saying tomorrow, and the fence was never painted.
senses.exampleCN: 他总说明天，篱笆却始终没有刷。
senses.why: Because the next day is always available in speech, tomorrow becomes the natural home of postponed promises.
senses.whyCN: 因为口语里永远还有下一个明天，tomorrow 就自然成了拖延承诺的落脚处。

senses.title: The next issue or edition
senses.definition: used in publishing for the edition that comes out on the next day
senses.definitionCN: 出版业中指第二天出的那一期
senses.example: The editor held the story for tomorrow's paper and let the evening edition go without it.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑把这条新闻留到明天的报纸，晚报就先不带它。
senses.why: Editors work a day ahead, so the next day's date in a masthead is simply the word for the coming edition.
senses.whyCN: 编辑总是提前一天工作，于是报头上第二天的日期就顺理成章成了「下一期」的代称。

senses.title: A future opportunity
senses.definition: a chance that will appear later rather than now
senses.definitionCN: 以后而不是现在才出现的机会
senses.example: There is always tomorrow, said the coach, meaning the next match.
senses.exampleCN: 教练说总还有明天，意思是还有下一场比赛。
senses.why: When a loss must be comforted, the next day becomes the name of hope itself.
senses.whyCN: 需要安慰一场失利时，下一天就成了希望这个名字。

senses.title: The future as a shared project
senses.definition: the future considered as something a group works towards together
senses.definitionCN: 被视为一个群体共同为之努力的未来
senses.example: The village meeting was really about tomorrow, not about the drains.
senses.exampleCN: 村会的真正议题是未来，而不是下水道。
senses.why: The word can stand for the whole horizon a community plans for, once it stops meaning one date.
senses.whyCN: 一旦不再指某个日期，这个词就能代表一个共同体规划的整片地平线。

senses.title: Time treated as an ordinary commodity
senses.definition: the next day as a plain unit of scheduling, without emphasis
senses.definitionCN: 作为普通日程单位的下一天，不带强调
senses.example: Tomorrow suits me better than Friday, if that is all right.
senses.exampleCN: 如果方便的话，明天比周五更适合我。
senses.why: Here the word carries no weight beyond the calendar, which is how it appears in most everyday planning.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词除了日历之外不携带任何分量，多数日常安排里它就是这样出现的。

senses.title: The adverb of the next day
senses.definition: as an adverb, on the day following today
senses.definitionCN: 作副词时指在今天之后的那一天
senses.example: She will drive north tomorrow and be back by Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 她明天开车北上，周日之前回来。
senses.why: The noun and the adverb share one shape, so the word sits in a sentence without any preposition at all.
senses.whyCN: 名词与副词同形，因此这个词可以不带任何介词直接进入句子。

intro.en: Tomorrow is a native English compound: the preposition to joined to morrow, an old word for the next day or the morning.
intro.cn: tomorrow 是英语本土复合词：介词 to 加上 morrow（古义为次日、早晨）。

items.en: The word morgen means morning, and morrow in the phrase on the morrow refers to the following day.
items.cn: 古英语 morgen 意为早晨，短语 on the morrow 里的 morrow 指紧接着的那一天。

items.en: To morgen, written as two words, points forward to the next morning and is the direct ancestor of the modern form.
items.cn: 写作两个词的 to morgen 表示「到明天早晨」，是现代形式的直接祖先。

items.en: The two elements merge into a single word to morwe, later tomorrow, while morrow keeps the older sense separately.
items.cn: 两个成分合并为一词 to morwe，后来成为 tomorrow，而 morrow 另行保留古义。

items.en: The word settles into its present spelling in the sixteenth century and takes over the adverbial use from the phrase on the morrow.
items.cn: 这个词在十六世纪定下现在的拼写，并接替短语 on the morrow 的副词用法。

items.en: From the eighteenth century tomorrow extends beyond the next day to mean the indefinite future.
items.cn: 十八世纪起，tomorrow 由「次日」扩展到指不确定的未来。

items.en: In modern speech it also stands alone as a promise or a postponement, as in tomorrow and tomorrow and tomorrow.
items.cn: 现代口语里它也单独用作承诺或拖延的说法，正如「明天，明天，再一个明天」那一句。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the other words of the same to- family in time words, while the near-meaning group gathers terms for the days and the future.
note.cn: 形近组收集时间词里由 to- 构成的同族词，近义组则汇集表示日期与未来的词。

entries.definition: on this present day
on this present night
the next day; in older use, morning
the dried leaves smoked or chewed
entries.definitionCN: 烟草，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the day before today
the time that has not yet come
at a time after now
the day that follows a given day

normalIntro.en: These memories use the two parts of the compound, the fixed time phrases, and the family with today and tonight.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用复合词的两个部分、固定时间短语，以及和 today、tonight 构成的词族。

normal.en: To plus morrow: the word literally means towards the next morning.
normal.cn: to 加 morrow：这个词字面意为「向着下一个早晨」。

normal.en: Tomorrow morning and tomorrow afternoon keep the noun before the time of day.
normal.cn: tomorrow morning 与 tomorrow afternoon 把名词放在具体时段之前。

normal.en: Today, tonight, and tomorrow all begin with to-, a small family for pointing at time.
normal.cn: today、tonight、tomorrow 都以 to- 开头，是专门指向时间的小词族。

normal.en: Morrow is the second half, and it survives alone in literary English.
normal.cn: morrow 是后半部分，在书面语里仍单独使用。

normal.en: There is no preposition: we say I will go tomorrow, not on tomorrow.
normal.cn: 这里不用介词：说 I will go tomorrow，而不是 on tomorrow。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pointing at a door that is still closed, and the closed door is tomorrow.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手正指向一扇还没打开的门，那扇门就是明天。

abstract.en: Think of a note left on the table that says only: tomorrow.
abstract.cn: 想桌上留了一张纸条，上面只写着：明天。

abstract.en: Every evening the word is handed back to you, empty again, ready to be filled.
abstract.cn: 每天傍晚这个词又被交还给你，空白如初，等着被填满。

examples.en: I will call you tomorrow after lunch.
examples.cn: 我明天午饭后给你打电话。

examples.en: Tomorrow's train leaves at six in the morning.
examples.cn: 明天的火车早上六点开。

examples.en: The planners kept talking about the city of tomorrow.
examples.cn: 规划者一直在谈未来的城市。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特玛柔」——拉着特玛柔的手说，明天再来，就是明天。

root: 古英语 to morgen（到明天早晨）→ 中古英语 to morwe → tomorrow。由介词 to 与 morrow（次日、早晨；古英语 morgen）合成；同族词有 today、tonight。

sensesIntro.en: The entry begins with the plain date that follows today, then widens to the near future, the old sense of morning, promises, editions, and finally the adverb that needs no preposition.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从紧接今天的那个日期写起，再扩到不久的将来、早晨的古义、承诺、报刊的一期，最后是不带介词的副词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pointing towards the next morning.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指指向下一个早晨。

branches.en: The next day as a date and as an ordinary schedule unit.
branches.cn: 作为日期与普通日程单位的下一天。

branches.en: The future as time, as opportunity, and as a shared project.
branches.cn: 作为时间、机会与共同事业的未来。

branches.en: The old sense of morning kept in greetings.
branches.cn: 在问候语里保留的早晨古义。

branches.en: The next day used to postpone.
branches.cn: 用来拖延的下一天。

branches.en: The next day in publishing and editions.
branches.cn: 出版领域里的次日一期。

intro.en: The word is a native compound of a preposition and a noun, and its endings are only the plural -s and its fixed time phrases.
intro.cn: 本词是介词与名词构成的本土复合词，可加的构词成分只有复数 -s 以及固定的时间短语。

items.example: The Old English word is the base of morrow.
items.exampleCN: 古英语这个词是 morrow 的基础。

items.example: The ending appears in both morrow and tomorrow.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾在 morrow 与 tomorrow 中都能看到。

items.example: Tomorrows means many days yet to come.
items.exampleCN: tomorrows 意为许多尚未到来的日子。

items.example: Today uses the same to- pattern.
items.exampleCN: today 使用同样的 to- 模式。

items.example: Tonight is built on the same model.
items.exampleCN: tonight 也按同一模式构成。

items.exampleCN: day 构成 today 的后半部分。

items.exampleCN: night 构成 tonight 的后半部分。

definition_zh: 吨；大量；许多；（船舶的）吨位
definition_en: a unit of weight of about a thousand kilograms, or a very large amount of something
core_image: 吊钩把一大捆钢锭慢慢放上货船的甲板
scene: 港口清晨，吊车把一捆捆钢材放上货轮，甲板被压得吱吱作响。The crane lifted a ton of steel onto the deck in a single swing.
sceneCN: 这里 ton 是重量单位「吨」（第 1 个义项：约一千公斤的重量单位）；句意为吊车一次就把一吨钢吊上甲板。画面里有货轮、吊钩与钢锭。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加复数词尾 -s 构成，义为「许多；大量」
由本词加名词后缀 -age 构成，义为「吨位；总吨数」
由本词加 -er 构成的复合成分，义为「……吨级的船或车」

senses.title: The unit of weight
senses.definition: a unit of weight equal to about one thousand kilograms, with several regional variants
senses.definitionCN: 约等于一千公斤的重量单位，各地有不同变体
senses.example: The lorry was carrying fifteen tons of sand.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆卡车装着十五吨沙子。
senses.why: The word is a spelling of tun, the great cask that once set the standard for what a ship could carry.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原是 tun（大酒桶）的拼法，那只大桶曾经规定了船只载重的标准。

senses.title: A very large quantity
senses.definition: an informally large amount of something that is counted by feel rather than by weight
senses.definitionCN: 口语中凭感觉估计的「很多」，而非实际称重
senses.example: I have tons of emails to answer before Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 周五之前我有一大堆邮件要回。
senses.why: Once a ton means a thousand kilos, saying tons becomes the easiest way to say a lot.
senses.whyCN: 一旦一吨意味着上千公斤，说 tons 就成了表示「很多」最省力的方式。

senses.title: The ton as a measure of a ship
senses.definition: a measure of the carrying capacity of a ship by volume rather than by weight
senses.definitionCN: 按容积而非重量衡量船舶载运能力的单位
senses.example: The ship is registered at six thousand tons and carries a crew of thirty.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘船登记吨位为六千吨，载有三十名船员。
senses.why: Ships were once rated by how many wine casks they could hold, so the cask became the ship's unit.
senses.whyCN: 船曾按能装多少桶酒来评级，于是那只桶就成了船的单位。

senses.title: A heavy blow or impact
senses.definition: used in phrases to describe a heavy or sudden shock
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语中描述沉重而突然的一击
senses.example: The news hit him like a ton of bricks.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息像一记重锤砸在他身上。
senses.why: A ton is a thousand kilos, so anything arriving like a ton of bricks is arriving with enormous weight.
senses.whyCN: 一吨是上千公斤，所以「像一吨砖那样砸下来」就是带着巨大重量到来。

senses.title: The imperial and American variants
senses.definition: the long ton of the British system and the short ton of the American one differ by about a hundred kilograms
senses.definitionCN: 英制长吨与美制短吨相差约一百公斤
senses.example: British lorries are rated in long tons while American freight is listed in short tons.
senses.exampleCN: 英国货车按长吨标定，而美国的货运单用短吨。
senses.why: Two systems inherited the same cask-based unit and then fixed it at different weights, so the spellings and the numbers both diverge.
senses.whyCN: 两套制度继承了同一个源于酒桶的单位，却把它定成不同的重量，于是拼法与数字都出现了分歧。

senses.title: The metric ton
senses.definition: the tonne of a thousand kilograms, now the standard unit in trade and science
senses.definitionCN: 即 tonne，一千公斤，如今是贸易与科学中的标准单位
senses.example: The contract specifies a metric ton, which avoids confusion between the older units.
senses.exampleCN: 合同写明用公吨，以免旧单位之间的混淆。
senses.why: Trade needed one shared figure, and the decimal ton supplied it by dropping the older barrels altogether.
senses.whyCN: 贸易需要一个共通的数字，公吨干脆抛开旧酒桶，正好提供了这个数字。

senses.title: Speed as an informal unit
senses.definition: used in idioms to mean a very fast speed, as in at a ton
senses.definitionCN: 在习语中表示极快的速度，如 at a ton
senses.example: The little motorbike came down the hill at a ton.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆小摩托以极快的速度冲下山坡。
senses.why: A hundred miles an hour was once the top of the scale, and the heaviest unit on hand was borrowed to mean the fastest speed.
senses.whyCN: 一小时一百英里曾是速度的上限，人们就借了手边最重的一个单位来表示最快。

senses.title: A great weight of feeling
senses.definition: the weight of a duty or a sorrow spoken of as if it could be weighed
senses.definitionCN: 把责任或悲伤说得仿佛可以称重
senses.example: He carried a ton of guilt about the missed call.
senses.exampleCN: 他对那个没接的电话背着一吨重的愧疚。
senses.why: Feelings are described with weights all the time, and the heaviest unit makes the metaphor as heavy as it can go.
senses.whyCN: 情感本来就常被说成重量，用最重的单位可以让这个比喻重到极点。

intro.en: The word is the same as tun, the large cask, and its history runs from wine barrels to ship capacity and finally to a plain weight.
intro.cn: 本词与 tun（大酒桶）同形同源，其历史从酒桶到船舶容量，最后落到一个平常的重量单位。

items.en: Late Latin tunna names a cask, probably borrowed from a Celtic word for a container.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 tunna 指酒桶，一般认为借自凯尔特语中表示容器的词。

items.en: Old French tonne keeps the sense of a large barrel and carries it into English.
items.cn: 古法语 tonne 保留大桶之义，并把这一含义带入英语。

items.en: English tun means a large cask, and tunne or ton is used for its capacity as a measure of wine.
items.cn: 中古英语 tun 意为大酒桶，tunne 或 ton 又用来表示桶的容量作为酒的计量。

items.en: A ship's size is stated in tons of cask capacity, which later shifts from volume to weight.
items.cn: 船的规模按「可装多少桶」的吨位陈述，这一用法后来由容积转向重量。

items.en: The weight ton of twenty hundredweight becomes standard in trade, with a British long ton and an American short ton.
items.cn: 二十英担的重量吨成为贸易标准，并分出英国长吨与美国短吨。

items.en: The metric ton of a thousand kilograms is now the international unit, though tons of in speech still just means a lot.
items.cn: 一千公斤的公吨如今是国际单位，而口语里的 tons of 仍然只是「许多」。

note.en: The look-alike group collects short words built on the same old cask and the units around it, while the near-meaning group gathers measures of weight and amount.
note.cn: 形近组收集由古酒桶一词以及周边单位构成的短词，近义组则汇集表示重量与数量的词。

entries.definition: a large cask, and the old measure of capacity
the total carrying capacity of a ship in tons
the metric ton of one thousand kilograms
entries.definitionCN: 公吨，拼写不同的同源词

entries.definition: a brown colour, or to make leather
entries.definitionCN: 棕褐色；鞣革，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the base metric unit of mass
a unit of weight of a hundred pounds or more
the amount that can be carried at once
a small unit of weight

normalIntro.en: These memories start from the cask behind the word, then use the unit family and the everyday idioms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条先从这个词背后的酒桶说起，再利用单位词族与日常习语。

normal.en: The word is tun, the wine cask, spelled with an o when it became a weight.
normal.cn: 这个词就是 tun，那只酒桶，在变成重量单位时改写成 o。

normal.en: Tons of is the spoken phrase for a lot, and the plural is what makes it informal.
normal.cn: tons of 是口语里的「很多」，用复数才显得随意。

normal.en: Tonnage adds -age and names a whole fleet's capacity.
normal.cn: tonnage 加 -age，指整个船队的总容量。

normal.en: A metric ton is a tonne, spelled with the -ne that marks the continental unit.
normal.cn: 公吨写作 tonne，那 -ne 是欧洲大陆单位的标记。

normal.en: A ton of bricks is a phrase about impact, not about construction.
normal.cn: a ton of bricks 说的是撞击，不是建筑。

abstract.en: Picture a crane cable going tight as a dark block of steel clears the dock.
abstract.cn: 想象吊索绷紧，一块黑沉沉的钢离开码头。

abstract.en: Think of a scale with a needle that swings once and stops far to the right.
abstract.cn: 想一台秤，指针荡了一下，停在最右边。

abstract.en: A ton is roughly what a small car weighs, so the word gives a body-sized sense of heaviness.
abstract.cn: 一吨大约是一辆小汽车的重量，所以这个词给重感一个身体尺度的想象。

examples.en: The truck can carry up to eight tons.
examples.cn: 这辆卡车最多能载八吨。

examples.en: They ordered a ton of gravel for the driveway.
examples.cn: 他们为车道订了一吨碎石。

examples.en: I have tons of reading to do this weekend.
examples.cn: 这个周末我有一大堆东西要读。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「桶」——一只大酒桶装满酒，正好压出一吨的重量。

root: 晚期拉丁语 tunna（酒桶，一般认为来自凯尔特语）→ 古法语 tonne → 中古英语 tun，后分化出 ton 表示重量与吨位；同族词有 tonnage、tonne。

sensesIntro.en: From one wine cask the entry spreads to a fixed weight, a ship's capacity, informal quantities, and finally to blows and burdens that feel as heavy as a ton.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一只酒桶出发，本词条目扩到固定的重量、船的容量、口语里的数量，最后是像一吨那么重的撞击与负担。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a great cask whose weight sets the standard.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只以其重量定标准的大酒桶。

branches.en: The unit of weight and its regional variants.
branches.cn: 重量单位及其地区变体。

branches.en: A large amount said without measuring.
branches.cn: 不做计量的「大量」。

branches.en: The capacity of a vessel in tons.
branches.cn: 船舶以吨计的容量。

branches.en: Impact and burdens measured by feel.
branches.cn: 凭感觉度量的撞击与负担。

branches.en: Very high speed in idiom.
branches.cn: 习语中的高速。

intro.en: The word is a single borrowed stem, and English builds only its plural, its -age noun, and many compounds.
intro.cn: 本词是单一借入词干，英语只加上复数、-age 名词以及若干复合成分。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entry shows the cask word from which the whole family descends.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁词条展示整个词族所由来的那只酒桶。

items.structure: Borrowed stem from Latin via French
items.example: The stem is unchanged in English.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干在英语中没有变化。

items.meaning: many units or an informal large amount
items.example: Tons of is the everyday phrase.

items.structure: Latin noun suffix used in English
items.example: Tonnage collects all the tons of a fleet.
items.exampleCN: tonnage 把一支船队所有吨数合在一起。

items.example: A ten-tonner is a ten-ton lorry.
Metric ton marks the continental standard.
items.exampleCN: metric ton 标明欧洲大陆标准。

items.example: A long ton is heavier than a short ton.
American freight uses the short ton.
Hundredweight is the older subdivision.
items.exampleCN: 英担是更早的细分单位。

items.meaning: to measure how heavy a thing is
items.example: A crate may weigh a ton.
items.exampleCN: 一只木箱可能重达一吨。

definition_zh: 音调；语调；语气；色调；腔调；使更有力；健身
definition_en: the quality of a sound or of a voice that shows feeling, or the shade of a colour, or the general character of something
core_image: 一根琴弦被拨动，绷出一声清亮的响，随后慢慢松开
scene: 老师在讲台上停下来，把声音放低，看着最后一排说话的学生。Her tone changed from friendly to formal the moment the noise began.
sceneCN: 这里 tone 是说话时的「语气」（第 2 个义项：语调传达的感情色彩）；句意为喧闹一开始，她的语气就从亲切变得正式。画面里有讲台、安静下来的教室与低下来的声音。

pos.zh: 动词：使（肌肉）结实；使更具力量

derivatives.zh: 由名词加 -al 构成，义为「音调的；色调的」
加 -less 构成，义为「单调的；没有感情色彩的」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「强身练习；色调处理」
加前缀 in- 与 -ation 构成的名词，义为「语调；声调」

senses.title: The pitch of a musical sound
senses.definition: the height or depth of a sound, measured by the speed of its vibration
senses.definitionCN: 声音的高低，由振动快慢决定
senses.example: The piano tuner tested each tone from the lowest string upward.
senses.exampleCN: 调音师从最低的弦开始，一个音一个音地试。
senses.why: The Greek root tonos means a stretching, as of a string, and a stretched string is what gives a tone its height.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词根 tonos 意为「拉紧」，就像绷紧的弦，而绷紧的弦正是音高的来源。

senses.title: The feeling carried by a voice
senses.definition: the quality of a voice that shows the speaker's attitude or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 说话人声音中流露的态度或感情
senses.example: Her tone told us the discussion was over.
senses.exampleCN: 她的语气告诉我们讨论到此为止。
senses.why: A stretched string has tension, and the voice carries a similar tension that listeners hear as attitude.
senses.whyCN: 绷紧的弦有张力，说话的声音也带着类似的张力，听者会把它听成态度。

senses.title: A shade of colour
senses.definition: a particular shade of a colour, or the general brightness of a picture
senses.definitionCN: 颜色的某一种深浅，或画面的整体明暗
senses.example: The walls were painted in warm tones of cream and sand.
senses.exampleCN: 墙壁被漆成奶油色与沙色这类暖色调。
senses.why: Painters speak of a picture's tonality, the overall balance of light and dark, and that language passed from music to colour.
senses.whyCN: 画家讲一幅画的「色调关系」即整体明暗平衡，这套说法是从音乐借到颜色上的。

senses.title: The spirit of a place or event
senses.definition: the general character or mood that something has
senses.definitionCN: 某事物整体的性质或气氛
senses.example: The chairman's opening remarks set the tone for the whole meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 主席的开场白为整场会议定下了基调。
senses.why: A gathering has a pitch of feeling the way a string has a pitch of sound, so the musical word shifts to mood.
senses.whyCN: 一场聚会的情感有音高，正如弦有音高，于是音乐用语转到了气氛上。

senses.title: Firmness of muscle
senses.definition: the healthy firmness of a muscle or of skin
senses.definitionCN: 肌肉或皮肤健康而有弹性的状态
senses.example: Regular swimming gave her arms a healthy tone.
senses.exampleCN: 经常游泳让她的手臂结实而有弹性。
senses.why: A muscle in good condition is under steady tension, the same tightness the Greek root named.
senses.whyCN: 状态良好的肌肉保持着稳定的张力，正是那个希腊词根所说的紧绷。

senses.title: To make something firmer
senses.definition: to make a muscle firmer, or to make a body more supple
senses.definitionCN: 使肌肉更结实，或使身体更柔韧
senses.example: Gentle exercises tone the back without straining it.
senses.exampleCN: 轻柔的运动能锻炼背部而不使其拉伤。
senses.why: The verb is formed directly from the noun of firmness, so the action is simply to produce that firmness.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词直接由表示结实的名词构成，动作就是产生那种结实。

senses.title: A difference of pitch in language
senses.definition: in some languages, a difference of pitch that changes the meaning of a word
senses.definitionCN: 在某些语言中，音高差别会改变词义的声调
senses.example: In that language the same syllable in a rising tone means a different thing entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 在那门语言里，同一个音节用升调就完全是另一个意思。
senses.why: Language uses the same small differences of pitch that music does, so a single word covers both systems.
senses.whyCN: 语言利用的正是音乐里那种微小的音高差别，于是一个词同时覆盖两套系统。

senses.title: To soften or moderate
senses.definition: to make a statement, colour, or sound less strong
senses.definitionCN: 使说法、颜色或声音变得不那么强烈
senses.example: The editor asked him to tone down the last paragraph.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑请他缓和一下最后一段的措辞。
senses.why: Turning a sound or a statement down lowers its pitch and volume, and the particle turns that image into a verb phrase.
senses.whyCN: 把声音或说法调低，就是降低它的音高与音量，这个小词把这一意象变成了动词短语。

senses.title: A telephone signal
senses.definition: the sound heard in a telephone receiver that shows the line is free or busy
senses.definitionCN: 从听筒中听到的声音，表示线路空闲或占线
senses.example: She lifted the receiver and waited for the dial tone.
senses.exampleCN: 她拿起听筒，等着拨号音。
senses.why: The steady hum of a free line is a single sustained pitch kept at one height, exactly what a tone is.
senses.whyCN: 空闲线路里那声平稳的嗡鸣就是一个保持在同一高度的持续音，正合 tone 之本义。

intro.en: Tone comes from Latin tonus, a stretching or tension, which in turn borrowed Greek tonos, and the musical sense grew out of the image of a tightened string.
intro.cn: tone 来自拉丁语 tonus（拉紧、张力），后者借自希腊语 tonos；音乐含义正是从「绷紧的弦」这一意象长出来的。

items.en: Tonos means a stretching or tightening, used of a bowstring, a rope, and later of the voice.
items.cn: 希腊语 tonos 意为拉紧、绷紧，用于弓弦、绳索，后来也用于嗓音。

items.en: Latin tonus keeps both the physical sense of tension and the musical sense of pitch.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tonus 同时保留「张力」的物理意义与「音高」的音乐意义。

items.en: Old French ton carries the word into the Romance speech of the Middle Ages with the sense of a musical sound.
items.cn: 古法语 ton 把这个词带入中世纪的罗曼语，含义为乐音。

items.en: English borrows tone in the thirteenth century for a musical note or the pitch of a voice.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 tone，指乐音或嗓音的音高。

items.en: By the eighteenth century tone extends to colours and to the mood of a gathering.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，tone 扩展到颜色与聚会的氛围。

items.en: The verb to tone, meaning to give firmness, appears later, and with down and up it becomes an everyday phrase.
items.cn: 表示「使之结实」的动词 tone 出现较晚，与 down、up 搭配后成了日常短语。

note.en: The look-alike group collects derivatives of the same stem, while the near-meaning group gathers words for sound quality and for mood.
note.cn: 形近组收集同一词干的派生词，近义组则汇集表示音质与气氛的词。

without expression or variety of pitch
the rise and fall of the voice in speech
a melody, or to adjust an instrument
entries.definitionCN: 曲调；调音，只是拼写相近，词源不同

the feeling that a place or event carries
a particular variety of a colour
the regular pattern of sounds or movements

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the stretched-string root, from the verb phrases with up and down, and from the colour senses.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从「绷紧的弦」这一词根、与 up 和 down 构成的动词短语，以及颜色义项入手。

normal.en: Tonos is a stretched string, so tone is the sound of tightness.
normal.cn: tonos 是一根绷紧的弦，所以 tone 就是紧绷发出的声音。

normal.en: Tone of voice is the phrase to keep when the sense is attitude.
normal.cn: 表示态度时，记住 tone of voice 这个搭配。

normal.en: Set the tone means fixing the mood at the outset, and the verb makes it an act.
normal.cn: set the tone 意为一开始就定下气氛，动词把它变成动作。

normal.en: Tone down lowers intensity, while tone up raises firmness, and the particle tells you which.
normal.cn: tone down 降低强度，tone up 提高结实度，小词说明方向。

normal.en: Tonal and toneless split the family into what has tone and what lacks it.
normal.cn: tonal 与 toneless 把词族分成「有声调」与「无声调」两路。

abstract.en: Picture a singer holding one note until the air in the room seems to stand still.
abstract.cn: 想象一位歌手拖住一个音，直到室内的空气仿佛静止。

abstract.en: Think of a lamp turned down one notch, and the whole room becomes a softer shade.
abstract.cn: 想一盏灯被调低一档，整个房间随之变成更柔的色调。

abstract.en: A voice can be a hand: soft on the shoulder, or flat on the table.
abstract.cn: 声音可以像一只手：轻轻搭在肩上，或重重拍在桌上。

examples.en: He answered in a calm tone of voice.
examples.cn: 他用平静的语气回答。

examples.en: The curtains are a light tone that makes the room look larger.
examples.cn: 窗帘是浅色调，让房间显得更大。

examples.en: She swims twice a week to tone her arms.
examples.cn: 她每周游两次泳来锻炼手臂线条。

sensesIntro.en: The entry starts with the pitch of a stretched string, then moves to the voice, to colour, to the spirit of an occasion, to muscle, to the verb phrases that soften or strengthen, and finally to the signal in a telephone.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从绷紧之弦的音高写起，再转到嗓音、颜色、场合的基调、肌肉、表示缓和与增强的动词短语，最后是电话里的信号音。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tightened string sounding at a fixed height.
core.cn: 核心意象：绷紧的弦在固定高度上发声。

branches.en: Pitch in music and in language.
branches.cn: 音乐与语言中的音高。

branches.en: The attitude carried by a voice.

branches.en: Brightness and shade in colour.

branches.en: The mood of an occasion and its adjustment.

branches.en: Muscle, the exercises that firm it, and the signal on a line.

definition_zh: 舌头；语言；口语；舌状物；鞋舌
definition_en: the soft movable organ inside the mouth used for tasting and speaking, or a language, or something shaped like a tongue
core_image: 张开的嘴里一条灵活的红舌，能尝味，也能卷出各种声音
scene: 医生让孩子张开嘴，用手电照着喉咙看了一眼。She burned her tongue on the first sip of the soup.
sceneCN: 这里 tongue 就是嘴里的「舌头」（第 1 个义项：口腔中能尝味的器官）；句意为她第一口汤就烫到了舌头。画面里有诊室的手电、孩子张开的嘴与一碗冒气的汤。

collocations.phrase: on the tip of one's tongue

derivatives.zh: 加复数词尾 -s，义为「多种语言」或「多条舌头」
加 -ed 构成复合形容词，义为「有……舌头的；说话方式……的」
加 -less 构成，义为「没有舌头的；沉默的」
合成形容词，义为「（紧张得）说不话的」

senses.title: The organ in the mouth
senses.definition: the soft muscular organ in the mouth that moves food and is used in tasting and speaking
senses.definitionCN: 口腔中柔软多肌的器官，用于搅拌食物、尝味与发音
senses.example: The dentist asked him to lift his tongue so the mirror could reach the back tooth.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医请他抬起舌头，好让镜子够到后面那颗牙。
senses.why: The word is one of the oldest in English and comes from a Germanic root that also gives the Latin and Greek names for the organ.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是英语最古老的词之一，来自日耳曼语词根，拉丁语与希腊语中称这个器官的词也与之同源。

senses.title: A language
senses.definition: a language, especially one spoken by a people or a region
senses.definitionCN: 语言，尤指某一民族或地区所说的语言
senses.example: He answered in his mother tongue, though the meeting was in English.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管会议用英语，他却用母语回答。
senses.why: The organ that makes words easily becomes the name for the whole system of words, as in many languages.
senses.whyCN: 造词的器官自然而然地成了整套词语系统的名字，许多语言都这样引申。

senses.title: The power of speech
senses.definition: the ability to speak, or a manner of speaking
senses.definitionCN: 说话的能力或说话的方式
senses.example: The shock loosened her tongue and she told the whole story.
senses.exampleCN: 震惊反倒让她开了口，把事情全说了出来。
senses.why: Speech depends on the tongue, so having a loose or a still tongue names the ability to speak or to hold back.
senses.whyCN: 言语有赖于舌头，因此「舌头松了」或「舌头不动」就用来指能说或忍住不说。

senses.title: An animal's long tongue
senses.definition: the long flexible organ of an animal, used for licking or catching food
senses.definitionCN: 动物长而灵活的舌状器官，用于舔食或捕捉食物
senses.example: The anteater flicks out its sticky tongue a hundred times a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 食蚁兽每分钟把黏舌弹出上百次。
senses.why: The same organ in other animals is often long and narrow, and English simply keeps the one word.
senses.whyCN: 其他动物的同一器官往往又长又窄，英语就沿用同一个词。

senses.title: Something shaped like a tongue
senses.definition: a strip or flap shaped like a tongue, such as the flap of a shoe
senses.definitionCN: 形如舌头的长条或薄片，如鞋舌
senses.example: Lift the tongue of the shoe before you pull it on.
senses.exampleCN: 穿鞋前先把鞋舌掀起来。
senses.why: A flat flap that lies inside something and moves when pulled looks like a tongue, so the name transfers by shape.
senses.whyCN: 一块藏在里面、一拉就动的薄片形似舌头，于是名字按形状转移过来。

senses.title: A strip of land or water
senses.definition: a narrow strip of land or water reaching out from a larger body
senses.definitionCN: 从较大地块或水体伸出的狭长部分
senses.example: A tongue of grey rock pushed out into the sea below the cliff.
senses.exampleCN: 一条灰色的舌状岩石从崖下伸入海中。
senses.why: Land and water shapes are named by resemblance, and a narrow projection looks like a tongue poking out.
senses.whyCN: 地块与水体的形状靠相似性命名，狭长的突起就像伸出的舌头。

senses.title: The needle of a balance
senses.definition: the moving pointer of a balance or gauge
senses.definitionCN: 天平或量表上会摆动的指针
senses.example: The tongue of the old scales swung and settled at the centre.
senses.exampleCN: 老秤的指针摆了几下，停在了中间。
senses.why: The pointer of a balance swings back and forth like a tongue and settles, so the instrument borrowed the name.
senses.whyCN: 天平的指针像舌头一样来回摆动继而停住，仪器就借用了这个名字。

senses.title: A clapper in a bell
senses.definition: the metal piece inside a bell that strikes the side to make the sound
senses.definitionCN: 钟内撞击钟壁发声的金属锤
senses.example: The bell hung silent, its tongue taken down for repair.
senses.exampleCN: 那口钟静静挂着，钟舌已被取下修理。
senses.why: The swinging metal piece that gives the bell its voice is the bell's tongue, named for what it does rather than its shape.
senses.whyCN: 那件摆动发声的金属正是钟的「舌」，命名依据是它的作用而非形状。

senses.title: Speech full of spite
senses.definition: sharp or unkind speech used to wound someone
senses.definitionCN: 用来伤人的尖刻言语
senses.example: Her mean tongue cleared the room faster than any shout.
senses.exampleCN: 她那刻薄的口舌比任何吼叫都能更快把人赶出屋子。
senses.why: Since the tongue makes words, a sharp tongue is a person's habit of cutting speech, and the organ stands for the habit.
senses.whyCN: 既然舌头造出言语，a sharp tongue 就是指说话刻薄的习惯，器官代指习惯。

intro.en: Tongue is an inherited English word from Old English tunge, whose Germanic root is related to the Latin and Greek words for the same organ.
intro.cn: tongue 是继承而来的英语词，来自古英语 tunge，其日耳曼语词根与拉丁语、希腊语中表示同一器官的词有亲缘关系。

items.en: Tunge means the organ of taste and speech, and the word is common in the earliest prose.
items.cn: 古英语 tunge 指尝味与说话的器官，在最早期的散文里已很常见。

items.en: The reconstructed stem tungo- is shared with Old Norse tunga and Old High German zunga.
items.cn: 可重构的词干 tungo- 与古诺斯语 tunga、古高地德语 zunga 同源。

items.en: The Latin word lingua, the Greek glossa, and the Germanic stem all descend from a very old common source, though their forms differ widely.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lingua、希腊语 glossa 与日耳曼语词干都出自一个非常古老的共同源头，只是形态差别很大。

items.en: Middle English tonge keeps both the bodily and the language senses, and the latter becomes the dominant one in writing.
items.cn: 中古英语 tonge 兼有身体器官与语言两义，书面语中后者逐渐占上风。

items.en: The spelling with a -ue ending is fixed in the fourteenth century, mostly under French influence on written forms.
items.cn: 以 -ue 结尾的拼写于十四世纪定型，多半受法语书面形态的影响。

items.en: The figurative senses develop quietly: the tongue of a shoe, of a bell, of a scale, and of the land.
items.cn: 比喻义悄然生长：鞋的舌、钟的舌、天平的舌，以及陆地的舌。

normal.en: Mother tongue is the phrase for the language learned first.
normal.cn: mother tongue 指最先学会的语言。

normal.en: A slip of the tongue is a small error in speech, not a fall.
normal.cn: a slip of the tongue 指说错话，而不是摔倒。

normal.en: In the phrase about the tip of the tongue, the word is almost recalled but not yet said.
normal.cn: 「话就在嘴边」这个说法里，词几乎想起来了却还没说出口。

normal.en: A shoe has a tongue and so does a bell, and both are flat pieces that move.
normal.cn: 鞋有舌，钟也有舌，两者都是会动的薄片。

abstract.en: Picture a red muscle curling into a cup to hold a drop of bitter medicine.
abstract.cn: 想象一条红色的肌肉卷成杯状，托住一滴苦药。

abstract.en: Think of a tongue of flame leaping sideways from a fire in the wind.
abstract.cn: 想一簇火舌被风拉向一侧。

abstract.en: The same organ that tastes soup also shapes every word you have ever spoken.
abstract.cn: 尝过汤的那个器官，也塑造了你说的每一个字。

examples.en: He bit his tongue while eating the hot pie.
examples.cn: 他吃热馅饼时咬到了舌头。

examples.en: Children learn their mother tongue long before they read it.
examples.cn: 孩子们在会读母语之前很久就学会说它了。

examples.en: The name of the street was on the tip of my tongue.
examples.cn: 那条街的名字就在我嘴边，一时却想不起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「烫」——舌头最怕烫，一烫就缩回去，可它偏又最会说话。

definition_zh: 今晚；今夜；今晚的（活动）
definition_en: the night or evening of the present day, or during that night
core_image: 街上灯一盏盏亮起来，剧场门口的灯箱写着今晚的场次
scene: 厨房里碗刚洗完，桌上还留着两杯热茶，窗外的天已经黑透了。The concert is tonight, so we should leave before seven.

senses.title: The night of today
senses.definition: the night or evening that follows the present day
senses.definitionCN: 今天之后的那个夜晚或傍晚
senses.example: We are staying in tonight because of the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 因为暴风雨，我们今晚待在家里。
senses.why: The word is a preposition fused to night, so it points at the dark part of the current day.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是介词与 night 的融合，指向当天的黑暗时段。

senses.title: During the coming night
senses.definition: as an adverb, during the night that follows today
senses.definitionCN: 作副词时指在今天之后的那一夜里
senses.example: The temperature will fall below zero tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚气温会降到零度以下。
senses.why: As an adverb the word needs no preposition, which is why we say tonight rather than in tonight.
senses.whyCN: 作副词时这个词不带介词，所以只说 tonight 而不说 in tonight。

senses.title: A scheduled event for today
senses.definition: the arrangement, programme, or performance set for the present evening
senses.definitionCN: 安排在今晚的活动、节目或演出
senses.example: Tonight's match has been moved to the smaller ground.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚的比赛已经改到较小的球场。
senses.why: With the possessive the word works as a noun, and that shift lets it label an event rather than a time.
senses.whyCN: 加所有格后它充当名词，这一转变使它能够标示一场活动而非一段时间。

senses.title: The present evening as a unit of plans
senses.definition: the present evening considered as the block of time available for plans
senses.definitionCN: 把今晚看作可用来安排事情的一段时间
senses.example: I have the whole of tonight to finish the chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 我有一整晚的时间读完这一章。
senses.why: Once it names a block of hours, the word can take quantity phrases like the whole of.
senses.whyCN: 一旦它指一段时辰，就能接 the whole of 这样的数量短语。

senses.title: The word in broadcasts
senses.definition: used in news and broadcasts to mark the report of the present day
senses.definitionCN: 新闻与广播中用来标明当天的报道
senses.example: Tonight we report on the election results from three regions.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚我们报道三个地区的选举结果。
senses.why: A broadcast must fix the day on which the listener hears it, so the word becomes a standard opening marker.
senses.whyCN: 广播必须钉住听众听到它的那一天，于是这个词成了标准的开场标记。

senses.title: An evening out
senses.definition: the evening's entertainment, especially when it is planned
senses.definitionCN: 今晚的娱乐活动，尤指事先安排好的
senses.example: Tonight is our anniversary dinner, so the whole family is coming.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚是我们的周年晚餐，全家人都来。
senses.why: In the phrase tonight is our dinner, the word stands in for the whole arrangement of the evening.
senses.whyCN: 在「今晚是我们的晚餐」这句话里，这个词代表整个晚上的安排。

senses.title: The coming night as a deadline
senses.definition: the present evening as the moment by which something must be done
senses.definitionCN: 把今晚当作某事必须完成的时刻
senses.example: The report has to be in tonight, or the printer will miss the morning edition.
senses.exampleCN: 报告今晚必须交，否则印刷厂会赶不上早报。
senses.why: Because the evening ends at midnight, the word can act as a deadline that is still ahead.
senses.whyCN: 因为夜晚到午夜就结束，这个词可以充当一个尚未到达的截止时刻。

senses.title: The word as a farewell
senses.definition: used in a farewell to mean that the speaker expects to meet again the same evening
senses.definitionCN: 道别时说，表示今晚还会再见
senses.example: See you tonight, she said, and closed the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她说了句今晚见，就把门关上了。
senses.why: A farewell can safely point at tonight because the same evening has still to happen.
senses.whyCN: 道别时可以放心指向今晚，因为这一晚还没发生。

intro.en: Tonight is a native compound of the preposition to and the noun night, built on the same model as today and tomorrow.
intro.cn: tonight 是介词 to 与名词 night 构成的本土复合词，其模式与 today、tomorrow 相同。

items.en: The phrase to niht, written as two words, means in or during this night.
items.cn: 古英语短语 to niht 写作两个词，意为今夜、在这夜里。

items.en: The two words begin to be written as one, toniht, and the sense narrows to the present evening.
items.cn: 两个词开始连写为 toniht，含义收窄为今晚。

items.en: The modern spelling tonight is fixed in the eighteenth century, at the same time as today takes its present form.
items.cn: 现代拼写 tonight 于十八世纪定型，与 today 定型的时间相同。

items.en: The noun use appears as soon as the compound is felt to be one word, as in the preparations for tonight.
items.cn: 一旦这个复合词被感觉成一个词，名词用法就出现了，如「为今晚做准备」。

items.en: Broadcasting gives the word a fixed function as a time marker at the start of reports.
items.cn: 广播让这个词固定承担在报道开头标示时间的职能。

items.en: In speech it also serves as a farewell, since the same evening is still to come.
items.cn: 口语里它还是道别语，因为那一晚还没过去。

note.cn: 形近组收集其余由 to- 构成的时间词，近义组则汇集表示一天各段与傍晚的词。

normal.en: Tonight's show uses the possessive to make the word act as a noun.

normal.en: See you tonight is a farewell because the evening has not passed yet.

normal.en: Late tonight and early tonight are both natural, proving the word can take a modifier.
normal.cn: late tonight 与 early tonight 都自然，说明这个词可被修饰。

abstract.en: Picture a stage lit against a dark street, with the audience still outside.
abstract.cn: 想象一座在暗街上亮起的戏台，观众还站在门外。

abstract.en: Think of the sky turning blue-black through a kitchen window while the kettle boils.
abstract.cn: 想水壶烧开时，厨房窗外的天正由蓝转黑。

abstract.en: Tonight is the smallest possible future: it begins in a few hours and ends by morning.
abstract.cn: 今晚是最小的未来：几小时后开始，天亮前结束。

examples.en: There is a film on television tonight.
examples.cn: 今晚电视上有一部电影。

examples.en: Tonight's dinner will be simple because we are late.

examples.en: Will you be free tonight to look at the plans?

definition_zh: 也；还；太；过于
definition_en: also, or more than is wanted or needed, or to a higher degree than is acceptable
core_image: 一只杯子里倒水，水面已经高过杯沿，再多一滴就要溢出来
scene: 试衣服的人站在镜子前拉了拉肩线，回头看了一眼同伴。The jacket is nice, but it is too tight across the shoulders.
sceneCN: 这里 too 表示「过于」（第 2 个义项：超过可接受程度）；句意为这件外套不错，但肩部太紧了。画面里有试衣镜、拉肩线的动作与同伴的眼神。

pos.zh: 副词：非常；很（口语中作加强）

senses.title: Also, in addition
senses.definition: as well, in addition to what has been mentioned, usually at the end of a clause
senses.definitionCN: 此外、同样地，通常位于句末
senses.example: She plays the violin, and she sings too.
senses.exampleCN: 她拉小提琴，也唱歌。
senses.why: The word is a stressed form of to, and the sense of addition grew out of the idea of going along with something.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 to 的重读形式，「也」的含义由「随之而去」的意思长出来。

senses.title: More than is wanted
senses.definition: to a greater degree than is suitable, pleasant, or acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 达到超出适宜、愉快或可接受的程度
senses.example: The soup is too salty to drink.
senses.exampleCN: 这汤太咸，喝不下去。
senses.why: Beyond is the second sense the Old English adverb carried, and it names the point where a limit has been passed.
senses.whyCN: 「超出」是古英语副词本来就有的第二个含义，它标示限度被越过的位置。

senses.title: Very, as an intensifier
senses.definition: in informal speech, a mild intensifier meaning very
senses.definitionCN: 口语中轻微的加强语，意为很
senses.example: I am not too sure about that plan.
senses.exampleCN: 我对那个计划不太有把握。
senses.why: Said with a falling voice, the word softens rather than sharpens, and that mild use is purely a habit of speech.
senses.whyCN: 压低语调说出时，它起缓和作用而非加强，这种轻微用法纯属口语习惯。

senses.title: A regretful excess
senses.definition: used to point at an excess that has unfortunate results
senses.definitionCN: 用来指出造成不幸结果的过头之处
senses.example: It was too late to change the ticket when we reached the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们到车站时，改签已经太晚了。
senses.why: Regret is what an excess leaves behind, so the word often appears in complaints about what is past changing.
senses.whyCN: 惋惜是「过头」留下的余味，所以这个词常出现在抱怨已无法改变之事的句子里。

senses.title: A polite refusal
senses.definition: used with a negative to soften a refusal or an apology
senses.definitionCN: 与否定词连用，使拒绝或道歉显得委婉
senses.example: It is not too far, if we take the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 如果坐公交，也不算太远。
senses.why: A negative before the word cancels the excess, which is how English makes a refusal sound gentler.
senses.whyCN: 在这个词前加否定就取消了「过头」，英语正是用这种方式让拒绝听起来温和。

senses.title: A comparison of degree
senses.definition: used before an adjective to show that a limit has been passed
senses.definitionCN: 放在形容词前，说明某项限度已被越过
senses.example: The room is too small for six chairs.
senses.exampleCN: 这房间太小，放不下六把椅子。
senses.why: The word always looks for an adjective or adverb to lean on, and that pairing is what makes a comparison of degree.
senses.whyCN: 这个词总要依附一个形容词或副词，这种搭配才构成程度上的比较。

senses.title: An emphatic agreement
senses.definition: in replies, an emphatic agreement with a negative or positive statement
senses.definitionCN: 在回应中表示强烈的赞同
senses.example: You were right. You were, too.
senses.exampleCN: 你说得对，确实对。
senses.why: In a reply the word can be added at the end to strengthen what the other person just said.
senses.whyCN: 在回应中把它加在句末，就能加强对方刚说过的话。

senses.title: A fixed adverbial phrase
senses.definition: used in set phrases to comment on frequency or degree
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定短语中评论频率或程度
senses.example: All too often the letter arrives after the meeting has ended.
senses.exampleCN: 信件往往在会议结束后才到。
senses.why: Fossil phrases keep old patterns alive, and all too often is a set comment on how frequently an excess happens.
senses.whyCN: 凝固短语让旧结构存活，all too often 就是一句固定的评论，说明某种过分之事发生得多频繁。

intro.en: Too is a stressed doublet of to, both descending from Old English to, and the sense of addition grew alongside the prepositional sense.
intro.cn: too 是 to 的重读同源形式，二者都来自古英语 to，「也」的含义与介词义并存发展。

items.en: To serves as preposition and adverb, covering towards, in addition, and beyond.
items.cn: 古英语 to 兼作介词与副词，涵盖「朝向」「此外」与「超出」等义。

items.en: The unstressed form to continues as the preposition, and the stressed form develops separately.
items.cn: 非重读形式 to 继续作介词，重读形式则单独发展。

items.en: The stressed form is written as to, too, or two, and the spelling settles as too in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 重读形式曾写作 to、too 或 two，拼写于十六世纪定为 too。

items.en: The sense of also becomes the common one, working in the same way as the German auch.
items.cn: 「也」成为最常见的义项，其功能与德语 auch 相似。

items.en: The excess sense is fixed in the phrases too much and too many, which become the standard counters of excess.
items.cn: 「过度」义固定在 too much 与 too many 两个短语里，成为表示过分的标准说法。

items.en: The informal intensifier use, as in not too bad, spreads in speech from the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 口语中「不太差」这类轻度加强用法自十八世纪起扩散。

note.cn: 形近组收集只差一个字母、容易拼错的词，近义组则汇集表示「也」与程度的副词。

normalIntro.cn: 下面几条把这个词的三个职能分开，并利用各自所在的固定短语。

normal.en: Too is a stressed to: one o more and one stress more, and the sense of addition turns into excess.
normal.cn: too 是重读的 to：多一个 o、多一分重音，「附加」就变成「过头」。

normal.en: Too comes at the end of a clause for also, but before an adjective for excess.
normal.cn: 表示「也」时位于句末，表示「过于」时位于形容词之前。

normal.en: Too much goes with uncountable nouns and too many with plural ones.
normal.cn: too much 接不可数名词，too many 接复数名词。

normal.en: Too ... to ... is the pattern of impossibility: too tired to walk.
normal.cn: too...to... 表示无法做到：太累而走不动。

normal.en: Me too is short for I think so too, and it drops the whole verb.
normal.cn: me too 是 I think so too 的省略，动词整个省掉了。

abstract.en: Picture a suitcase that closes only when someone sits on it, and that is too full.
abstract.cn: 想象一只得坐上去才关得上的箱子，那就是「太满」。

abstract.en: Think of one more guest arriving at a table that already has every chair taken.
abstract.cn: 想一张椅子已坐满的桌子又来了一位客人。

abstract.en: Too is the word for the moment a good thing crosses the line into a problem.
abstract.cn: too 就是好事越过界线变成问题那一刻的词。

examples.en: He works in the city and teaches at weekends too.

examples.en: There were too many people in the small hall.
examples.cn: 小礼堂里人太多了。
