scene: 木工台面上散着凿子、卷尺和几块未刨的木料，墙上的木板插满了带柄的工具。He laid each tool back in its place before turning off the light.
sceneCN: 这里 tool 是「工具」这一类物件（第 1 个义项：手持以帮助工作的器物）；句意为他在关灯前把每件工具都放回原位。画面里有木工台、凿子、卷尺与墙上挂满工具的木架。

pos.zh: 动词：用工具加工；给……装上工具

derivatives.zh: 加复数词尾 -s，义为「工具（复数）」
由 tool 与 kit 合成，义为「工具套装；方法组合」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「模具工装；加工」
由 tool 与 box 合成，义为「工具箱」

senses.title: An object made to help with work
senses.definition: a device, usually held in the hand, that is made to do a job more easily
senses.definitionCN: 通常手持的器具，制成以后使工作更容易完成
senses.example: A good spade is the only tool you need for this bed.
senses.exampleCN: 这块花圃只需要一把好铲子这件工具。
senses.why: The word is one of the oldest in English, and the earliest senses cover any instrument of labour.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是英语最古老的词之一，最早的义项涵盖任何劳作器械。

senses.title: A means of achieving something
senses.definition: anything used by a person or group to reach an end
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体用来达到目的的任何东西
senses.example: Language is the chief tool of the historian.
senses.exampleCN: 语言是历史学家的主要工具。
senses.why: Anything that extends what a person can do counts as an instrument, so the word moves easily from metal to method.
senses.whyCN: 任何能扩展人所能做之事的东西都算器械，所以这个词很自然地从金属移到方法。

senses.title: A person used by another
senses.definition: someone who is used by others to do their work or to carry out their plans
senses.definitionCN: 被他人利用来做事或实现其计划的人
senses.example: He was a tool of the men who really ran the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 他不过是真正操控委员会那些人手里的工具。
senses.why: A person who merely carries out another's purpose is treated like an implement, and the metaphor is deliberately unkind.
senses.whyCN: 只是实现他人目的的人被当成器物，这个比喻是刻意刻薄的。

senses.title: A set of software functions
senses.definition: a program or function that helps carry out a specific task
senses.definitionCN: 帮助完成某项特定任务的程序或功能
senses.example: The new tool lets you compare two versions of the same document.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新工具可以比较同一文档的两个版本。
senses.why: Software repeats the oldest pattern in the language: a thing made to make work easier, this time without metal.
senses.whyCN: 软件重复了语言里最古老的一套用法：为使工作更易而造出的东西，只是这回没有金属。

senses.title: The cutting part of a machine
senses.definition: the cutting or shaping part of a machine, such as a drill bit
senses.definitionCN: 机床中切削或成形的部件，如钻头
senses.example: Change the tool before the edge dulls completely.
senses.exampleCN: 在刃口完全变钝之前换掉刀具。
senses.why: A machine works by cutting with a tool, so the cutting part inherits the name of the hand tool it replaced.
senses.whyCN: 机器靠刀具切削工作，于是这个切削部件继承了他所取代的手持工具之名。

senses.title: To shape with tools
senses.definition: to cut, shape, or decorate something with a tool
senses.definitionCN: 用工具切割、成形或装饰某物
senses.example: The leather was tooled with a small floral pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 这块皮革用小花纹压出了图案。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into an action: to work a material with a tool until a pattern appears.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：用工具加工材料，直到出现花纹。

senses.title: To equip for work
senses.definition: to provide a workshop or factory with the tools it needs
senses.definitionCN: 为作坊或工厂提供所需的工具
senses.example: The plant was tooled up for a new model in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂在春季为一种新车型配齐了工装。
senses.why: Equipping a plant is giving it tools at industrial scale, and the same verb covers the workshop and the shop floor.
senses.whyCN: 给工厂装备工具就是工业规模上的「给工具」，同一个动词兼指车间与流水线。

senses.title: To drive a vehicle
senses.definition: in informal speech, to drive a vehicle, especially steadily along
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指开车，尤指平稳前行
senses.example: We tooled along the river road all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 我们整个下午沿着河边公路开车闲逛。
senses.why: The slang sense treats a car as the tool of the journey and the driving as working it along.
senses.whyCN: 俚语义把汽车当作旅程的工具，开车就是把这件工具一路使过去。

senses.title: A plain phrase in computing
senses.definition: a small program run from a command line to perform one task quickly
senses.definitionCN: 在命令行运行以快速完成单项任务的小程序
senses.example: A single command-line tool replaced three old scripts.
senses.exampleCN: 一个命令行工具就取代了三个旧脚本。
senses.why: Computing names its small single-purpose programs tools because each one does one job well in the hand.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域把单项用途的小程序称作工具，因为每一件就在手中把一件事做好。

intro.en: Tool is an inherited Germanic word, recorded in Old English as tol, and its prehistory beyond the Germanic languages is uncertain.
intro.cn: tool 是继承的日耳曼语词，古英语记作 tol，其在日耳曼语系之外的更早来源尚不确定。

items.en: Tol is used of any instrument or implement, including weapons and writing implements.
items.cn: 古英语 tol 用于任何器械或工具，包括武器与书写用具。

items.en: The stem tolam is shared with Old Norse tol and related forms meaning an implement.
items.cn: 词干 tolam 与古诺斯语 tol 以及表示工具的若干同源形式共有。

items.en: Middle English tool spreads to cover hand tools of every trade and keeps the general sense of a means.
items.cn: 中古英语 tool 扩展到各种手艺的手持工具，并保留「手段」的一般含义。

items.en: The verb appears in the nineteenth century, first for shaping by hand and later for fitting a factory with machines.
items.cn: 动词用法出现于十九世纪，先指手工成形，后指为工厂配备机器。

items.en: The slang sense of a person used by others is recorded from the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 「被人利用的人」这一俚语义自十六世纪有记录。

items.en: Computing borrows the word for programs, and software tools become one of the commonest uses today.
items.cn: 计算机领域借用这个词指程序，软件工具成了今天最常见的用法之一。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds and near spellings, while the near-meaning group gathers words for instruments and for means.
note.cn: 形近组收集复合词与近似拼写，近义组则汇集表示器具与手段的词。

entries.definition: a set of tools, or a set of methods
a box for keeping tools
the tools and equipment needed for manufacture
also, or excessively
entries.definitionCN: 也；太，只是拼写近似，词源不同

entries.definition: a device used for careful work, often medical or musical
a simple tool used out of doors or in a trade
a machine made for a particular purpose
a tool used in a kitchen or household

normalIntro.en: These memories use the Old English word, the compounds with box and kit, and the way the word slides from objects to means to software.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用古英语原词、与 box 和 kit 构成的复合词，以及这个词由实物滑向手段再到软件的过程。

normal.en: Old English tol is short and plain, and it still names anything that helps you work.
normal.cn: 古英语 tol 简短朴素，至今仍指任何帮着干活的东西。

normal.en: Toolbox and toolkit add box and kit, and both mean a container plus what is in it.
normal.cn: toolbox 与 toolkit 分别加 box 与 kit，都表示容器及其中的东西。

normal.en: A tool for doing something is the abstract sense, and for signals it.
normal.cn: a tool for doing something 是抽象义，介词 for 明确标示。

normal.en: Power tools are driven by motors, and the modifier tells you the power source.
normal.cn: power tools 由电机驱动，修饰语说明动力来源。

normal.en: Software tools borrow the plain word because a good program feels like a well-kept hammer.
normal.cn: 软件工具借用这个朴素的词，因为一个好程序像一把保养良好的锤子。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching without looking for the hammer that is always in the same place.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手不看就伸向那柄永远放在原处的锤子。

abstract.en: Think of a simple blade that turns a difficult job into an easy one.
abstract.cn: 想一件简单的刃具，把难活变成易活。

abstract.en: A tool is a hand made harder, longer, or sharper by design.
abstract.cn: 工具是被设计得更硬、更长或更锐利的手。

examples.en: Please put the tools back in the box when you finish.
examples.cn: 做完以后请把工具放回箱子里。

examples.en: Statistics are a tool, not an answer in themselves.
examples.cn: 统计是一种工具，本身不是答案。

examples.en: The workshop was tooled for bicycle frames only.
examples.cn: 那家车间只配备了生产自行车车架的工装。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「图」——做工程先看图纸，再动手拿工具。

root: 古英语 tol（器具、工具），日耳曼语同源词干 tolam；更早来源不确定。含义由实物器具扩展到抽象手段，二十世纪又扩展到软件工具。

sensesIntro.en: The entry begins with the object in the hand, then reaches for means, for people used by others, for the cutting edge of a machine, and finally for the programs and the verb senses that grew from the same plain word.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从手中的器物写起，继而伸向手段、被利用的人、机床的刃口，最后是同一个朴素词形长出的软件与动词义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worn handle in the hand that makes work possible.
core.cn: 核心意象：手中被磨旧的握柄，使工作得以完成。

branches.en: The object in the hand and the cutting part of a machine.
branches.cn: 手中之物与机床的刃口。

branches.en: Means, software functions, and command-line programs.
branches.cn: 手段、软件功能与命令行程序。

branches.en: A person treated as an instrument.
branches.cn: 被当作器械的人。

branches.en: The verb of shaping and of equipping.
branches.cn: 表示成形与配备的动词用法。

branches.en: The slang verb for driving.
branches.cn: 表示开车的口语动词。

intro.en: The word is a short Germanic stem with almost no affixes; its growth is by compounding with box, kit, and bar.
intro.cn: 本词是简短的日耳曼语词干，几乎不带词缀，其扩展主要靠与 box、kit、bar 等合成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for the word itself; the Latin entries below belong to borrowed relatives such as instrument.
latinIntro.cn: 本词本身没有拉丁语来源；下列拉丁词条属于 instrument 一类借入的亲属词。

items.example: The stem is unchanged in spelling.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干拼写没有变化。

items.example: The Old English form has one l.
items.exampleCN: 古英语形式只有一个 l。

items.example: Tools is the plural.
Tooled leather is shaped leather.
items.exampleCN: tooled leather 指压花成形的皮革。

items.example: Tooling can mean the tools of a plant.
Toolbox keeps the tools together.

items.meaning: a set of things for one purpose
items.example: Toolkit is often used figuratively.
Toolbar names the strip of buttons on a screen.
items.exampleCN: toolbar 指屏幕上的按钮条。

items.example: Power tools replaced many hand tools.
items.exampleCN: 电动工具取代了许多手工工具。

latinEntries.meaning: a tool, an implement, an instrument

definition_zh: 牙；牙齿；齿状物；（齿轮的）齿
definition_en: one of the hard white parts in the mouth used for biting and chewing, or a pointed part shaped like one
core_image: 一排白牙咬住硬纸的边角，发出清脆的一声
scene: 灯下照着镜子里张开的口，牙刷停在最后一颗臼齿上。He brushed each tooth slowly, counting them as he went.
sceneCN: 这里 tooth 就是嘴里的「牙齿」（第 1 个义项：口腔中用于咀嚼的坚硬白色器官）；句意为他把每颗牙慢慢刷过去，边刷边数。画面里有镜子、牙刷与张口的动作。

pos.zh: 名词：齿状物；（齿轮等的）齿

derivatives.zh: 不规则复数形式，义为「牙齿（复数）」
加 -less 构成，义为「无牙的；不起作用的」
加 -y 构成，义为「露齿的；牙齿显眼的」
与 ache 合成，义为「牙痛」

senses.title: The white part in the mouth
senses.definition: one of the hard calcified structures set in the jaws and used for biting and chewing
senses.definitionCN: 嵌在上颌与下颌中的坚硬钙化结构，用于咬与咀嚼
senses.example: The dentist found a small crack in the back tooth.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医在后面一颗牙上发现了一条小裂缝。
senses.why: The word is inherited from Old English toth, with a Germanic plural that changes the vowel to teeth.
senses.whyCN: 这个词继承自古英语 toth，其日耳曼语的复数通过元音变化成 teeth。

senses.title: A pointed part of a tool
senses.definition: a projecting part on a comb, a saw, a gear, or a zip
senses.definitionCN: 梳子、锯、齿轮或拉链上凸出的部件
senses.example: One tooth of the zip was bent out of line.
senses.exampleCN: 拉链上有一个齿歪出了线。
senses.why: A comb or a saw works exactly as the mouth does, gripping or cutting with small hard points, so the same word serves.
senses.whyCN: 梳子或锯的工作方式与嘴相同，都是用小而硬的尖端去抓或切，于是同一个词就沿用了。

senses.title: A liking for a kind of food
senses.definition: in informal speech, a liking for a particular kind of food or activity
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示对某种食物或活动的偏好
senses.example: She has a sweet tooth and never refuses pudding.
senses.exampleCN: 她爱吃甜食，从不拒绝布丁。
senses.why: A craving feels like something in the mouth that wants to bite, so the phrase gives appetite a tooth of its own.
senses.whyCN: 馋意就像嘴里有个想咬东西的部件，于是这个说法也给食欲安上了一颗牙。

senses.title: A tooth in phrases of retaliation
senses.definition: used in the old legal phrase an eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth
senses.definitionCN: 用于「以眼还眼、以牙还牙」这一古老法律短语中
senses.example: The old code demanded a tooth for a tooth, but the new one asks for payment.
senses.exampleCN: 旧律条要求以牙还牙，新法典只要求赔偿。
senses.why: The law of equal revenge names the injured part itself, so losing a tooth is repaid by a tooth.
senses.whyCN: 对等报复的律条直接点出受伤的部位，所以失去一颗牙就以一颗牙偿还。

senses.title: The hard surface that does work
senses.definition: the part of something that grips, cuts, or bites down
senses.definitionCN: 某物中起抓握、切割或咬合作用的部位
senses.example: The clamp has worn teeth that no longer hold the pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 夹具的齿磨平了，再也夹不住管子。
senses.why: The point that bites down is the part that does the work, so the word spreads to any gripping surface.
senses.whyCN: 真正用力的是那个咬下去的点，于是这个词扩展到任何起抓握作用的面。

senses.title: Age shown by the teeth
senses.definition: used in phrases that judge age from the state of the teeth, as with horses
senses.definitionCN: 用于按牙齿状况判断年龄的短语，如对马
senses.example: Judging by the tooth, the horse is older than the seller says.
senses.exampleCN: 从牙齿看，这匹马比卖主说的年纪大。
senses.why: Teeth wear in a fixed order, so a farmer reads age in them the way one reads a calendar.
senses.whyCN: 牙齿按固定次序磨损，农人看牙如同看日历一样读出年龄。

senses.title: A child growing a tooth
senses.definition: the emergence of a first tooth in a baby
senses.definitionCN: 婴儿第一颗牙长出
senses.example: The baby cut her first tooth at seven months and chewed everything after that.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子七个月时出了第一颗牙，此后什么都想咬。
senses.why: The first tooth is the child's first tool, so cutting it marks the start of eating solid food.
senses.whyCN: 第一颗牙是孩子拥有的第一件工具，它长出来便标志着开始吃固体食物。

senses.title: The unpleasantness of a task
senses.definition: used in the phrase get one's teeth into to mean dealing with hard work properly
senses.definitionCN: 用于 get one's teeth into，表示认真对付难事
senses.example: The new project finally gave her something to get her teeth into.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新项目终于让她有了一件可以狠下功夫的事。
senses.why: Hard work is treated as food that needs biting, so sinking the teeth in means committing fully.
senses.whyCN: 难事被当作需要咬住的食物，所以把牙扎进去就是全力投入。

intro.en: Tooth is one of the oldest words in English, from Old English toth, with relatives in every Germanic language and a very old Indo-European root behind them.
intro.cn: tooth 是英语最古老的词之一，来自古英语 toth，在所有日耳曼语中都有亲属词，其背后还有一个非常古老的印欧词根。

items.en: Toth names the biting organ, and the plural tech changes the vowel, a pattern still kept in teeth.
items.cn: 古英语 toth 指咬噬器官，复数 tech 通过元音变化构成，这一模式至今保存在 teeth 里。

items.en: Old Norse tenn, Old High German zan, and Gothic tunthus all trace back to one Germanic stem.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 tenn、古高地德语 zan 与哥特语 tunthus 都可上溯到同一个日耳曼语词干。

items.en: The Latin dens and the Greek odous belong to the same very old Indo-European family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dens 与希腊语 odous 属于同一个非常古老的印欧语族。

items.en: The spelling moves through toth and tothe, and the modern form loses the final vowel sound.
items.cn: 拼写经历 toth 与 tothe 等形态，现代形式丢掉了末尾的元音。

items.en: The word extends early to pointed parts of tools, since a saw tooth bites wood as a tooth bites bread.
items.cn: 这个词很早扩展到工具的尖齿，因为锯齿咬木头正如牙齿咬面包。

items.en: Expressions like sweet tooth and a tooth for a tooth fix the word in proverb and in idiom.
items.cn: sweet tooth 与 a tooth for a tooth 这类说法把这个词固定在谚语与习语里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds and derivatives built on the word, while the near-meaning group gathers the parts and products of the mouth.
note.cn: 形近组收集由本词构成的复合词与派生词，近义组则汇集口腔部位及相关物。

without teeth, or without real power
pain in a tooth
a small enclosed space or stall
entries.definitionCN: 小间；摊位，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the firm pink flesh around the teeth
either of the two bones that hold the teeth
a long sharp tooth of an animal

normalIntro.en: These memories use the irregular plural, the compounds with ache and brush, and the tool sense that grew from biting.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用不规则复数、与 ache 和 brush 等构成的搭配，以及由「咬」生长出的工具义。

normal.en: The plural is teeth, not tooths, and the vowel change is the same one in foot and feet.
normal.cn: 复数是 teeth 而不是 tooths，这个元音变化与 foot 变 feet 相同。

normal.en: Toothache adds ache to tooth, and the compound is written as one word.
normal.cn: toothache 由 tooth 加 ache，写成一体。

normal.en: A sweet tooth is an appetite for sugar, and the phrase treats the liking as a body part.
normal.cn: a sweet tooth 指爱吃甜食，这个说法把偏好当作一个身体部件。

normal.en: A tooth for a tooth is the oldest legal formula the word appears in.
normal.cn: a tooth for a tooth 是这个词出现的最古老法律套语。

normal.en: A saw has teeth because it bites wood, which is why tools borrow the word.
normal.cn: 锯有齿是因为它咬木头，工具正是因此借用了这个词。

abstract.en: Picture a hard white ridge flashing behind a laugh and then gone.
abstract.cn: 想象笑时露出一道坚白的棱，随即又消失。

abstract.en: Think of gears meshing, each ridge falling into the gap of the next wheel.
abstract.cn: 想齿轮咬合，每个齿落进另一个轮的凹槽。

abstract.en: A tooth is the only part of the body you see being used as a tool every day.
abstract.cn: 牙齿是身体里唯一每天当工具用的部件。

examples.en: The child lost a front tooth and laughed at the gap.
examples.cn: 孩子掉了一颗门牙，对着那个缺口笑。

examples.en: Two teeth on the large gear are worn away.
examples.cn: 大齿轮上有两个齿已经磨损。

examples.en: He has a sweet tooth and keeps chocolate in his desk.
examples.cn: 他爱吃甜食，抽屉里总放着巧克力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「凸」——牙是嘴里最硬、最凸出的那一排。

root: 古英语 toth（复数 tech）→ 现代 tooth（复数 teeth）。日耳曼语同源词有古诺斯语 tenn、古高地德语 zan；更远处与拉丁语 dens、希腊语 odous 同族。

sensesIntro.en: The entry begins with the biting organ, follows the same shape into combs, saws, and gears, and then collects the idioms in which a tooth stands for appetite, for revenge, and for age.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从咬噬器官写起，再顺着同一形状走入梳、锯与齿轮，然后汇集那些用「牙」表示食欲、报复与年龄的习语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard white ridge made for biting.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排为咬合而生的坚硬白棱。

branches.en: The tooth itself and the cutting of a first tooth.
branches.cn: 牙齿本身与第一颗牙的长出。

branches.en: Pointed parts that grip or cut.
branches.cn: 起抓握或切割作用的尖部。

branches.en: Liking for a kind of food.
branches.cn: 对某种食物的偏好。

branches.en: The old law of equal revenge.
branches.cn: 对等报复的古老律条。

branches.en: State of the teeth as age, and hard work as biting.
branches.cn: 以牙齿状况示年龄，以咬喻硬功夫。

intro.en: The word is a short inherited stem, so its family grows by vowel change, -less, -y, and compounds with ache and brush.
intro.cn: 本词是简短的继承词干，其词族靠元音变化、-less、-y 以及与 ache、brush 等的合成扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give dens and its derivatives, the other branch of the same very old family.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁词条给出 dens 及其派生词，那是同一古老族系的另一支。

items.example: The stem is unchanged since Old English.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干自古英语以来没有变化。

items.example: The Old English form ends in th.
items.exampleCN: 古英语形式以 th 结尾。

items.example: Feet and teeth share the same plural pattern.
items.exampleCN: feet 与 teeth 的复数模式相同。

items.example: Toothless means without teeth.
Toothy describes a wide smile.
Toothache is pain in a tooth.

items.meaning: a brush for a stated use
items.example: A toothbrush is for the teeth.
Toothpaste is used with the brush.
Sweet tooth names a liking for sugar.

definition_zh: 顶部；顶端；盖子；首位；上衣；最上面的；顶部的；超过
definition_en: the highest part or point of something, or the best position, or the covering of a container
core_image: 一只手扶住梯子最上面那一级，脚下是整片屋顶
scene: 爬完最后一节梯子，屋顶就在眼前，风比街上大得多。From the top of the hill you can see the whole harbour.
sceneCN: 这里 top 是「顶部、最高处」（第 1 个义项：物体的最高部分）；句意为从山顶上你能看到整个港湾。画面里有梯子顶端的横档、屋顶与远处的港湾。

pos.zh: 形容词：最上面的；最高的；顶尖的

derivatives.zh: 加复数词尾 -s，义为「顶部（复数）」，口语中也可作形容词「顶尖的」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「（食物上的）浇头；配料」
加 -less 构成，义为「无顶的；无上装的」
加最高级 -most 构成，义为「最上的；最高的」

senses.title: The highest part
senses.definition: the highest point or part of a thing
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的最高处或最高部分
senses.example: A small flag was fixed to the top of the pole.
senses.exampleCN: 杆子的顶端系着一面小旗。
senses.why: The plain physical sense is the base from which lid, rank, and verb all later develop.
senses.whyCN: 这个最朴素的物理义项，是后来盖子、名次与动词各项含义所由发展的基础。

senses.title: A lid or cover
senses.definition: the cover of a container or bottle
senses.definitionCN: 容器或瓶子的封盖
senses.example: Screw the top back on before you shake it.
senses.exampleCN: 摇之前先把盖子拧回去。
senses.why: A lid closes a vessel at its top, so the word for the highest part names the cover too.
senses.whyCN: 盖子在容器顶端封口，于是表示最高部分的词也用来指盖子。

senses.title: The best or highest position
senses.definition: the leading place in a group, a list, or a profession
senses.definitionCN: 在群体、名单或行业中的领先位置
senses.example: She finished the season at the top of the rankings.
senses.exampleCN: 她在赛季结束时排名榜首。
senses.why: A ranking is a vertical list, so the person at the highest point of it is at the top.
senses.whyCN: 排名是一张竖着的名单，位于其最高点的人就在 top。

senses.title: A garment for the upper body
senses.definition: a piece of clothing worn on the upper body
senses.definitionCN: 穿在上身的衣物
senses.example: He put on a clean top and went down to dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他换上一件干净的上衣下楼吃饭。
senses.why: A top is the garment on the upper half of the body, and the word simply reuses the idea of the upper part.
senses.whyCN: top 指穿在上半身的衣物，这个词只是再次动用了「上部」这一概念。

senses.title: The highest in rank
senses.definition: as an adjective, highest in rank, quality, or position
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词时指等级、质量或位置最高的
senses.example: The matter is a top priority for the whole department.
senses.exampleCN: 这件事是整个部门的头等大事。
senses.why: The adjective is formed from the noun without any ending, which is common for short English words.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词直接由名词构成，不加任何词尾，这对英语短词很常见。

senses.title: To be higher than
senses.definition: to be greater in amount or degree than something else
senses.definitionCN: 在数量或程度上高出另者
senses.example: Sales topped two million copies in the first month.
senses.exampleCN: 首月销量超过了两百万册。
senses.why: A figure is like a mark on a pole, and to pass above it is to top it.
senses.whyCN: 一个数字像杆上的刻度，越过去就是 top it。

senses.title: To cover the surface of
senses.definition: to put something on the upper surface of food or of a structure
senses.definitionCN: 在食物或结构的上表面加上某物
senses.example: She topped the cake with thin slices of lemon.
senses.exampleCN: 她在蛋糕上铺了薄薄的柠檬片。
senses.why: Topping a dish is putting something on its upper surface, and the cooking verb keeps the meaning literal.
senses.whyCN: 给菜加浇头就是在它的上表面放东西，这个烹饪动词保留了字面意义。

senses.title: The head in informal speech
senses.definition: in informal speech, the head or hair on it
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指头顶或其上的头发
senses.example: He took his cap off and scratched the top of his head.
senses.exampleCN: 他摘下帽子挠了挠头顶。
senses.why: The informal head sense descends from the old word for a tuft of hair on the crown.
senses.whyCN: 口语中的「头顶」义来自那个表示头顶发簇的古词。

senses.title: A spinning toy
senses.definition: a toy that spins on a point, an older sense kept in the word's history
senses.definitionCN: 一种以尖端着地旋转的玩具，是这个词较早的义项
senses.example: The spinning toy is a separate word that happens to share the spelling, and it survives in the modern language only in this narrow use.
senses.exampleCN: 这种旋转玩具有自己的词源，只是恰好同形，今天只在极窄的用法里留存。
senses.why: The toy turns on a single point at its bottom, so the shape of a top on a point links the two words by accident of form.
senses.whyCN: 陀螺以底部的一个尖点旋转，于是「尖顶」之形与它偶然相连，成了同形的两个词。

intro.en: Top is an Old English word for the highest part, and an older separate sense names a spinning top; the two senses were probably never the same word.
intro.cn: top 在古英语中表示最高部分；另一个更早的义项指陀螺，两者很可能从来不是同一个词。

items.en: Top names the summit or the highest point, and is used of hills, trees, and buildings.
items.cn: 古英语 top 指顶巅或最高点，用于山、树与建筑。

items.en: A separate word topp names a tuft of hair on the head, which explains the informal sense of the head.
items.cn: 另有一个词 topp 指头上一簇头发，这解释了口语中「头顶」的义项。

items.en: Old Norse toppr and Old High German zopf all mean a summit or a tuft.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 toppr 与古高地德语 zopf 都表示顶或发簇。

items.en: Middle English applies top to lids and covers, since a lid sits at the top of a vessel.
items.cn: 中古英语把 top 用于盖子，因为盖正位于容器的顶上。

items.en: The verb to top appears in the sixteenth century with the sense of putting something on the upper surface.
items.cn: 动词 top 于十六世纪出现，义为在表面之上放东西。

items.en: The sense of surpassing comes in the seventeenth century, from the idea of going above a mark.
items.cn: 「超过」之义于十七世纪出现，源自越过某个标记的想法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects short forms built on the same stem, while the near-meaning group gathers words for summit, cover, and ranking.
note.cn: 形近组收集同一词干构成的短形式，近义组则汇集表示顶部、盖子与名次的词。

normalIntro.en: These memories use the fixed phrases with on and at, the compounds, and the way the word turns into an adjective and a verb.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用与 on、at 的固定搭配、复合词，以及这个词转为形容词与动词的路径。

normal.en: Top of is a position, on top of is contact, and the particle changes the picture.
normal.cn: top of 是位置，on top of 是接触，介词改变了画面。

normal.en: Top priority puts the adjective before the noun and means first in importance.
normal.cn: top priority 把形容词放在名词前，意为最重要。

normal.en: From top to bottom goes through a thing completely, from the first layer to the last.
normal.cn: from top to bottom 从第一层到最后一层，指彻底贯穿。

normal.en: Bottle top and pen top both mean the cover, because a cover sits where the top is.
normal.cn: bottle top 与 pen top 都指盖子，因为盖就在顶处。

normal.en: The verb to top means to rise above a figure, as in sales topped a million.
normal.cn: 动词 top 意为高于某个数字，如销量过百万。

abstract.en: Picture a hand flat on the very last rung, with nothing above it but sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按在最后一级横档上，上面只剩天空。

abstract.en: Think of a list where one name sits alone above all the others.
abstract.cn: 想一张名单，有一个名字单独居于所有名字之上。

abstract.en: A top closes a thing, ranks a thing, and beats a thing, and all three come from being highest.
abstract.cn: 顶能封住一物、排出一物、也高过一物，三者都源自「在最上」。

examples.en: There is a bird's nest at the top of the tree.
examples.cn: 树顶有一个鸟巢。

examples.en: The bottle top rolled under the table.
examples.cn: 瓶盖滚到桌子下面去了。

examples.en: The film topped the box office for three weeks.
examples.cn: 这部电影连续三周位居票房榜首。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「托」——顶上要托住，托在最上面的就是 top。

root: 古英语 top（顶巅），另有 topp（头顶发簇）；日耳曼语同源词有古诺斯语 toppr、古高地德语 zopf。由「最高处」引申出盖子、首位、超过等义。

sensesIntro.en: The entry starts from the highest part of a thing, then takes in lids, leading positions, clothing, and finally the adjective and verb that have grown from the same image.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从物体的最高处写起，继而收进盖子、领先地位、上衣，最后是同一意象长出的形容词与动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the highest point, with nothing above it.
core.cn: 核心意象：最高点，其上再无他物。

branches.en: The highest part and, informally, the head.
branches.cn: 最高部分，以及口语中的头顶。

branches.en: The cover and the act of covering.
branches.cn: 盖子与覆盖的动作。

branches.en: Leading place and the adjective of rank.
branches.cn: 领先地位与表示等级的形容词。

branches.en: The garment that goes on top.
branches.cn: 穿在上身的衣物。

branches.en: Rising above a figure.
branches.cn: 高过某个数字。

intro.en: The word is one short stem; its family comes from -ing, -less, -most, and compounds with table, bottle, and roof.
intro.cn: 本词是一个短词干，其词族来自 -ing、-less、-most，以及与 table、bottle、roof 等合成。

latinIntro.en: No Latin ancestor exists for this native word, so only related loanwords are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 本词是本土词，没有拉丁语祖先，故只列出相关的借词。

items.example: Topping is food put on top.

Topmost is the highest of all.
Tops serves both noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: tops 兼作名词复数与动词三单。

items.example: Tabletop is a common compound.
Rooftop names the top of a building.
Bottle top is the everyday word.

definition_zh: 话题；题目；主题；议题
definition_en: the subject of a talk, a piece of writing, or a discussion
core_image: 黑板正中写着一行大字，全班的讨论都围绕它展开
scene: 会议白板上只写了一句话，其余地方都空着，主持人指着它让大家发言。The topic for today's seminar is how cities treat their rivers.
sceneCN: 这里 topic 是讨论的「主题」（第 1 个义项：谈话或写作的主题）；句意为今天研讨会的主题是城市如何对待自己的河流。画面里有白板、一句话和围坐的人。

pos.zh: 名词：（写作或研究的）选题

derivatives.zh: 加复数词尾 -s，义为「多个话题」
加 -al 构成，义为「时事性的；当前相关话题的」
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「就话题而言；按时事地」
由形容词加 -ity 构成，义为「时事性」

senses.title: The subject of a discussion
senses.definition: the subject that a talk, an article, or a meeting is about
senses.definitionCN: 谈话、文章或会议所围绕的主题
senses.example: The speaker changed the topic when the questions became personal.
senses.exampleCN: 问题一涉及私事，讲者就换了话题。
senses.why: The word names the ground the whole exchange stands on, so to change it is to move to different ground.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指整场交流所立足的那块地，换掉它就是移到另一块地上。

senses.title: A subject for writing
senses.definition: a subject chosen for an essay, a report, or a piece of research
senses.definitionCN: 为论文、报告或研究所选的主题
senses.example: Her topic was the effect of noise on birds in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 她的选题是噪音对城市鸟类的影响。
senses.why: A writer must choose one place among many, and that chosen place is called a topic.
senses.whyCN: 写作者要从许多地方里选出其一，而选定的那一处就叫 topic。

senses.title: A heading in a list
senses.definition: one of the items or headings into which a course or a list is divided
senses.definitionCN: 课程或清单划分出的一个条目
senses.example: The course covers twelve topics, from soil to water quality.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课涵盖十二个主题，从土壤到水质。
senses.why: When a course is divided, each division gets a heading, and each heading inherits the name of a place of argument.
senses.whyCN: 课程被切分时，每一块都有一个标题，而每个标题都继承了「论证所在」这个名字。

senses.title: A subject of public interest
senses.definition: a matter that many people are discussing at present
senses.definitionCN: 当前许多人都在谈论的事情
senses.example: A place becomes crowded when everyone gathers there, so a hot topic is literally a crowded place of talk.
senses.exampleCN: 当所有人聚到一处，那个地方就拥挤起来，所以热门话题字面上是谈话拥挤之地。
senses.why: Once the Greek place word became a subject word, any subject people crowd around could be called hot.
senses.whyCN: 一旦那个希腊「地方」之词变成了「主题」之词，任何众人聚拢的主题都能被称作 hot。

senses.title: A separate matter on the table
senses.definition: one distinct item for decision among several
senses.definitionCN: 若干待决事项中独立的一项
senses.example: Housing is the first topic on the agenda tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 住房是今晚议程上的第一项议题。
senses.why: An agenda is a row of places to visit, and each one is a topic.
senses.whyCN: 议程是一串要依次到访的地点，每一处都是一个 topic。

senses.title: The subject of a study
senses.definition: the central subject around which a study or an investigation is built
senses.definitionCN: 一项研究或调查所围绕的中心主题
senses.example: Choosing a narrow topic makes the reading manageable.
senses.exampleCN: 把主题选窄，阅读量就变得可控。
senses.why: Research needs a single ground that can be covered, so the word means the chosen field of a study.
senses.whyCN: 研究需要一块能走完的地面，所以这个词也指一项研究所选定的领域。

senses.title: A conversation opener
senses.definition: a light subject used to begin a conversation
senses.definitionCN: 用来开始交谈的轻松话题
senses.example: Weather is the safest topic with strangers.
senses.exampleCN: 和陌生人聊天，天气是最安全的话题。
senses.why: A safe topic is neutral ground where neither speaker risks an argument.
senses.whyCN: 安全的话题是中立的地面，双方在那儿都不会引发争执。

senses.title: A topic in a text
senses.definition: the subject a passage is organised around, often named in a topic sentence
senses.definitionCN: 一段文字所组织的主题，常由主题句点明
senses.example: The topic of the paragraph is announced in its first sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 这一段的话题由它的第一句点明。
senses.why: A paragraph must announce its ground before building on it, and that announcing sentence takes the name of the word.
senses.whyCN: 一段文字必须先声明它立足的地面，再在其上建构，这个声明句就用了本词之名。

intro.en: Topic comes from the Greek word for place, topika, used of the places of argument in Aristotle's logic; English extended the word from the headings of an argument to any subject.
intro.cn: topic 来自希腊语中表示「地方」的 topika，原指亚里士多德逻辑里论证的「所在」；英语把它从论证的条目扩展到任何主题。

items.en: Topos means a place, and ta topika are the places or common headings from which arguments are drawn.
items.cn: 希腊语 topos 意为地方，ta topika 指抽取论证的「所在」或通用条目。

items.en: Latin topica names the same collection of argument headings, and the word enters learned Latin as a title.
items.cn: 拉丁语 topica 指同一套论证条目，作为书名进入学术拉丁语。

items.en: Old French topic descends from the Latin title and is used of a general heading of thought.
items.cn: 古法语 topic 源自这一拉丁书名，用于表示一般性的思想条目。

items.en: English takes topic in the sixteenth century for a common heading of argument, then for any subject.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 topic，先指论证的常用条目，后指任何主题。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the modern sense of the subject of a talk is ordinary.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，「谈话主题」这一现代义项已很平常。

items.en: Topical and topically grow from it to mean what is currently discussed or locally applied.
items.cn: topical 与 topically 由它派生，意为当前所讨论的，或局部施用的。

note.en: The look-alike group collects derivatives of the same stem, while the near-meaning group gathers words for subject, argument, and the point under discussion.
note.cn: 形近组收集同一词干的派生词，近义组则汇集表示主题、论点与讨论焦点的词。

the plural of the word

normalIntro.en: These memories start from the Greek word for place, then use the fixed phrases of discussion and writing.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从希腊语中表示「地方」的词说起，再利用讨论与写作的固定搭配。

normal.en: The Greek topos means a place, so a topic is the ground a discussion stands on.
normal.cn: 希腊语里的 topos 就是「地方」，所以 topic 是讨论所立足的地面。

normal.en: Change the topic means to leave that ground and step onto another.
normal.cn: change the topic 意为离开那块地，踏到另一块上。

normal.en: A topic sentence announces the ground of a paragraph in its first line.
normal.cn: topic sentence 在第一行就点明一段的地面。

normal.en: Topical news is news about what people are discussing now.
normal.cn: topical news 就是关于人们当下议论之事的新闻。

normal.en: On the topic of is the formal bridge into a subject.
normal.cn: on the topic of 是正式引入某个主题的桥。

abstract.en: Picture a single line of chalk on a blackboard with the whole class facing it.
abstract.cn: 想象黑板上一行粉笔字，全班都朝着它。

abstract.en: Think of a table where one card has been laid face up and the rest are still covered.
abstract.cn: 想一张桌子，一张牌已翻开，其余还盖着。

abstract.en: A topic is a place people can stand together, which is why the old word was simply a place.
abstract.cn: 话题是人们可以一起站的地方，所以那个古词本来就是「地方」。

examples.en: Let us return to the topic of the budget.
examples.cn: 让我们回到预算这个话题。

examples.en: Climate change is a hot topic among students this year.
examples.cn: 气候变化今年在学生中是个热门话题。

examples.en: The first sentence of the paragraph states the topic clearly.
examples.cn: 这一段的第一句清楚地表明了主题。

sensesIntro.en: From a Greek place of argument the word became the subject of a talk, then the choice of a writer, the item on an agenda, and the light opening of a conversation.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从希腊语中「论证的所在」变成了谈话的主题，又变成写作者的选题、议程上的一项、以及谈话的轻松切入点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a place where a discussion stands.
core.cn: 核心意象：讨论所立足的一处地面。

branches.en: What a conversation is about, and how it starts.

branches.en: A subject chosen for writing or research.

branches.en: Items into which a course or agenda is divided.

definition_en: a stick with burning material at one end, used as a light, or in American English a small electric light held in the hand
core_image: 夜里一支火把压得很低，火焰被风吹得偏向一侧
scene: 队伍沿着山路向上去看日出，最前面的人举着火把照路。A guide with a torch led the way through the cave.
sceneCN: 这里 torch 是照明用的「火把/手电」（第 1 个义项：手持的照明器具）；句意为一名拿着火把的向导领着大家穿过洞穴。画面里有山路、洞口与前进的队伍。

pos.zh: 动词：（口语）故意纵火；烧毁

derivatives.zh: 加复数词尾 -es，义为「火把（复数）」
与 light 合成，义为「火光；手电光」
与 bearer 合成，义为「持火炬者；传承者」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「纵火；焚烧」

senses.title: A stick that burns as a light
senses.definition: a piece of wood or other material with a flame at one end, used to give light
senses.definitionCN: 一端燃着火焰的木棒或其他材料，用来照明
senses.example: The villagers walked to the shrine with torches in their hands.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们手持火把走向神庙。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the burning bundle itself, and everything else in English is drawn from it.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意义就是那束燃烧的东西本身，英语里的其余义项都从它引出。

senses.title: A small electric light
senses.definition: in British English, a small battery lamp carried in the hand
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语中指手持的小型电池灯
senses.example: He took a torch from the drawer and went down to the cellar.
senses.exampleCN: 他从抽屉里拿出手电，下到地窖去了。
senses.why: British English keeps the old word for the new lamp, since both are portable hand-held lights.
senses.whyCN: 英式英语用旧的词指新的灯，因为两者都是手持的便携光源。

senses.title: A flame carried in relays
senses.definition: a symbolic flame carried from place to place, as at the Olympic games
senses.definitionCN: 在各地之间传递的象征性火焰，如奥运会火炬
senses.example: The torch was carried through the town by runners of all ages.
senses.exampleCN: 火炬由各年龄段的跑者传递穿过城镇。
senses.why: A relay flame is a torch that changes hands instead of going out, so the word becomes a symbol of continuity.
senses.whyCN: 接力的火焰是一支换了手却不熄灭的火把，于是这个词成了延续性的象征。

senses.title: The flame of a burning building
senses.definition: a fire set deliberately to destroy a building
senses.definitionCN: 为毁掉建筑而故意点燃的火
senses.example: The old mill was put to the torch during the unrest.
senses.exampleCN: 动乱中那座老磨坊被付之一炬。
senses.why: To put something to the torch is to give it up to the flame, a phrase that turns the light into a weapon.
senses.whyCN: 把某物交给火把，就是任其被焚，这个短语把光源变成了武器。

senses.title: A guide in the dark
senses.definition: something that gives light or understanding when all else is dark
senses.definitionCN: 在其余一切皆暗时给出光亮或理解的东西
senses.example: Her letters were a torch in the difficult winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那些信是艰难冬天里的一支火把。
senses.why: The image of the only light in a dark place makes the word natural for help and understanding.
senses.whyCN: 「暗处唯一的光」这一形象让这个词顺理成章地用于帮助与理解。

senses.title: A flame of devotion
senses.definition: used in the phrase carry a torch to mean holding an unreturned love
senses.definitionCN: 用于 carry a torch，表示怀有得不到回应的爱慕
senses.example: A flame that is kept burning inside and shown to no one is exactly the shape of a love not returned.
senses.exampleCN: 一簇在内里持续燃烧却不给任何人看的火，正是得不到回应的爱的形状。
senses.why: The phrase keeps the whole torch, flame and carrier together, because the lover is the one who holds the light.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把火把、火焰与持火者一并保留下来，因为爱慕者正是那个举着光的人。

senses.title: To set fire deliberately
senses.definition: in informal speech, to set fire to something on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指故意放火烧某物
senses.example: Someone torched the empty shed behind the school.
senses.exampleCN: 有人放火烧了学校后面那座空棚屋。
senses.why: The verb simply reverses the noun: what was a source of light becomes a means of destruction.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词只是把名词翻转：本来是光源的东西变成了毁灭的手段。

senses.title: A craft of flame in ritual
senses.definition: the burning light carried in processions and ceremonies
senses.definitionCN: 游行与仪式中被举着燃烧的光
senses.example: Each autumn the torch was lit at the top of the tower.
senses.exampleCN: 每年秋天，塔顶上的火把都会被点燃。
senses.why: Ritual keeps the oldest sense in full view: a flame that is carried, watched, and expected each year.
senses.whyCN: 仪式把最古老的意义完整保留：一簇每年被举着、被看着、被期待的火。

intro.en: Torch comes through Old French from Latin torqua or torca, a twisted thing, from the verb torquere, to twist, because a torch was a twist of fibre soaked in pitch.
intro.cn: torch 经古法语来自拉丁语 torqua 或 torca（绞成的东西），源于动词 torquere（扭、绞）；因为火把就是把纤维绞紧再浸上沥青。

items.en: Torquere means to twist or turn, and the derived noun names a twisted bundle.
items.cn: 拉丁语 torquere 意为扭、转，其派生名词指绞成的一束。

items.en: Torqua or torca names a twisted cord or a wreath, and the sense of a twisted firebrand develops from it.
items.cn: torqua 或 torca 指绞成的绳或花环，表示绞成之火炬的义项由此发展。

items.en: Old French torche is a twisted bundle of waxed or pitched fibre used as a light.
items.cn: 古法语 torche 指用蜡或沥青浸过的绞紧纤维束，用作照明。

items.en: English borrows torch in the thirteenth century for a portable light carried in the hand.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 torch，指可以手持携带的光源。

items.en: With the arrival of batteries the word is applied to a small electric lamp in British usage.
items.cn: 电池出现以后，英式用法把这个词用于小型电灯。

items.en: The figurative senses of passing the torch and carrying a torch are fixed in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: pass the torch 与 carry a torch 等比喻用法在十九至二十世纪定型。

note.en: The look-alike group collects other words built on the same twisting root, while the near-meaning group gathers kinds of light.
note.cn: 形近组收集建立在同一「扭绞」词根上的其他词，近义组则汇集各种光源。

normal.en: In Britain a torch is a flashlight, which surprises many American readers.

normal.en: Carry a torch for someone means loving without being loved back.

normal.en: Torque is the same root in engineering, a twisting force.

abstract.en: Picture one small flame moving along a dark road, with ten people following it.

abstract.en: Think of a hand cupped around a flame to keep the wind off.

abstract.en: A torch is light that someone else is carrying for you, which is why it stands for guidance.

definition_zh: 折磨；酷刑；拷打；极度痛苦；使受折磨
definition_en: the act of causing severe pain to punish or force a confession, or great mental suffering
core_image: 绳索被绞紧，一具身体在绳子另一端绷得笔直
scene: 牙科诊室外的长椅上，患者捏着挂号单，听见里面机器的声音就皱起眉。Waiting three hours for a reply was pure torture.
sceneCN: 这里 torture 是精神上的「折磨」（第 2 个义项：极度的痛苦煎熬）；句意为等回信的三个小时简直是纯粹的折磨。画面里有诊室外的长椅、捏紧的单子与紧锁的眉。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「受折磨的；（文体）矫揉的」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「施酷刑者」
加 -ous 构成，义为「折磨人的；曲折痛苦的」
同根形容词，义为「曲折的；拐弯抹角的」

senses.title: The deliberate infliction of pain
senses.definition: the act of causing severe physical pain to a person, often to punish or to extract information
senses.definitionCN: 为使某人受罚或招供而故意造成剧烈肉体痛苦的行为
senses.example: The treaty forbids torture under any circumstances.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约禁止在任何情况下使用酷刑。
senses.why: The legal sense is the oldest one in English, and international law still uses the word in exactly this way.
senses.whyCN: 这个法律义项是英语里最早出现的，国际法至今仍按这一含义使用该词。

senses.title: Severe mental suffering
senses.definition: great suffering of the mind, caused by worry, guilt, or waiting
senses.definitionCN: 由忧虑、内疚或等待造成的巨大精神痛苦
senses.example: The weeks before the results came out were torture for the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 结果公布前的几周对全家都是折磨。
senses.why: Pain that is not physical still feels inflicted, so the old word for bodily torment moves into the mind.
senses.whyCN: 非身体的痛苦仍像是被人施加的，于是那个老旧的肉体折磨之词转入了心灵。

senses.title: Something that causes suffering
senses.definition: a thing or situation that is extremely unpleasant to endure
senses.definitionCN: 极难忍受的事物或处境
senses.example: That traffic on Friday evenings is absolute torture.
senses.exampleCN: 周五傍晚的那段交通简直是折磨。
senses.why: Everyday things that cannot be escaped often take the strongest available word, and this is one of the strongest.
senses.whyCN: 无法逃避的日常之事常借用手上最强的词，而这正是一个很强的词。

senses.title: To cause pain to someone
senses.definition: to inflict pain on a person, physically or mentally
senses.definitionCN: 在肉体或精神上给某人造成痛苦
senses.example: He was tortured by doubt for months before deciding.
senses.exampleCN: 决定之前，他被疑虑折磨了好几个月。
senses.why: The verb allows both a physical agent and an abstract one, which is why doubt can torture a person.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词既可接实在的施动者，也可接抽象者，所以「疑虑」也能折磨一个人。

senses.title: To twist the meaning of words
senses.definition: to force a word or idea into a sense it does not naturally carry
senses.definitionCN: 把一个词或观念硬扭成它本来没有的意思
senses.example: Do not torture the sentence into meaning the opposite of what it says.
senses.exampleCN: 不要把这个句子曲解成与它原意相反的意思。
senses.why: Meaning can be bent out of shape as a body can, which brings the word back to its twisting root.
senses.whyCN: 意义可以像身体一样被扭得变形，这又把这个词带回它「扭」的词根。

senses.title: The historical instrument of law
senses.definition: the use of pain as a legal instrument in past legal systems
senses.definitionCN: 过去法律体系中把疼痛当作法律手段的做法
senses.example: Records show that torture was used to obtain confessions in that court.
senses.exampleCN: 档案显示那个法庭曾用刑讯逼取口供。
senses.why: In legal history the word names an admitted procedure, which is what makes it valuable in reading old records.
senses.whyCN: 在法律史上这个词曾指一种被承认的程序，读旧档案时正因如此才需要它。

senses.title: The writer's strained style
senses.definition: in the phrase tortured style, language that is forced and unnatural
senses.definitionCN: 在 tortured style 这一说法中，指勉强而不自然的文笔
senses.example: The translation reads in a tortured style that hides the plain sense.
senses.exampleCN: 这份译文文笔矫揉，把明白的意思藏了起来。
senses.why: Style that is forced is like a rope pulled too far, so the same adjective serves both pain and prose.
senses.whyCN: 强扭的文风就像拉得太过的绳，于是同一个形容词兼用于痛苦与文笔。

senses.title: The metaphor of the twisted rope
senses.definition: the underlying image of something twisted out of its natural shape
senses.definitionCN: 底层意象是某物被扭离其自然形态
senses.example: The road tortures itself around the mountain through a dozen hairpins.
senses.exampleCN: 那条路绕山拐了十几个急弯。
senses.why: The noun keeps the physical image in the background, while the adjective tortuous shows it plainly.
senses.whyCN: 名词把物理意象留在背景里，而形容词 tortuous 把它明明白白地呈现出来。

intro.en: Torture comes from Latin tortura, a twisting, from torquere, to twist; the sense moved from bending the body out of shape to pain inflicted on purpose.
intro.cn: torture 来自拉丁语 tortura（扭绞），源于 torquere（扭）；其义从把身体扭得变形，转到故意施加的痛苦。

items.en: Torquere means to twist or bend, and tortura is a twisting, used of ropes under strain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 torquere 意为扭、弯，tortura 是扭绞本身，用于受力的绳索。

items.en: In legal Latin tortura names the application of force to make a person speak.
items.cn: 在法律拉丁语中，tortura 指施加暴力以逼人开口。

items.en: Old French torture carries the legal sense of judicial tormentation into medieval courts.
items.cn: 古法语 torture 把司法拷问的法律含义带入中世纪法庭。

items.en: English borrows torture in the fifteenth century, first as a legal term and then more widely.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 torture，先作为法律术语，后扩展到更广的用法。

items.en: The mental sense, as in the torture of waiting, becomes common in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 「等待的折磨」这类精神意义在十八世纪普遍起来。

items.en: The older physical image survives in tortuous, the adjective for a winding road, and in the mechanics of torque.
items.cn: 古老的物理意象保存在 tortuous（形容蜿蜒之路）与力学中的 torque 里。

note.cn: 形近组收集同一「扭绞」词根的亲属词，近义组则汇集表示痛苦与残暴的词。

causing great pain
a twisting force
extreme pain of body or mind
the state of undergoing pain

normalIntro.en: These memories use the twisting root shared with torque and tortuous, the two senses of body and mind, and the phrase be tortured by.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用与 torque、tortuous 共有的「扭绞」词根、身心两个义项，以及 be tortured by 这一搭配。

normal.en: The root is twist, so torture is a body or a mind twisted out of its shape.
normal.cn: 词根是「扭」，所以折磨就是把身体或心思扭得变形。

normal.en: Torture, torque, and tortuous share the twist, and their meanings tell you which way it went.
normal.cn: torture、torque、tortuous 共用「扭」，各自的含义说明它扭向了哪边。

normal.en: Be tortured by doubt is the common passive pattern for the mental sense.
normal.cn: be tortured by doubt 是精神义常用的被动态。

normal.en: Sheer torture and mental torture both take the noun as an uncountable mass.
normal.cn: sheer torture 与 mental torture 都把名词当作不可数的整体。

normal.en: Tortured style means forced writing, which is the same twist applied to language.
normal.cn: tortured style 指矫揉的文笔，就是把同样的扭力施加到语言上。

abstract.en: Picture a rope pulled tight until it hums, and then pulled further.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳被拉紧到发出嗡声，然后又被拉。

abstract.en: Think of a clock face you cannot stop watching while you wait for news.
abstract.cn: 想一张你等消息时无法不看的钟面。

abstract.en: Torture is imposed pain, and the word keeps the memory that it was once done with ropes.
abstract.cn: 酷刑是被施加的痛，这个词保存着它曾用绳索实施的记忆。

examples.en: The prisoners were held for weeks without charges or torture of any kind.
examples.cn: 这些被拘留者数周未受指控，也没有遭受任何形式的酷刑。

examples.en: He was tortured by the memory of what he had said.
examples.cn: 他被自己所说过的话的记忆折磨着。

examples.en: The long bus ride was torture for the children.
examples.cn: 漫长的长途汽车之旅对孩子们是种折磨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「同扯」——两人同扯一根绳，扯得生疼，就是折磨。

root: 拉丁语 torquere（扭、绞）→ tortura（扭绞；刑讯）→ 古法语 torture → 英语 torture。同根词有 torque、tortuous、tort。

sensesIntro.en: The entry begins with the deliberate infliction of pain, then moves to the suffering that is not physical, to the verb of tormenting, and at last back to the twisting image that started it: twisted words, twisted roads, and twisted style.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从故意施加的痛苦写起，再到非身体的苦痛、表示折磨的动词，最后回到最初的「扭」这一意象：扭曲的词、蜿蜒的路与矫揉的文风。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something pulled or twisted out of its natural shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：被拉扯、扭离其自然形态之物。

branches.en: Pain inflicted deliberately, by law or by force.
branches.cn: 由法律或暴力故意施加的痛苦。

branches.en: Suffering of the mind and the things that cause it.
branches.cn: 精神苦痛及其来源。

branches.en: The verb of tormenting or being tormented.
branches.cn: 折磨或被折磨的动词用法。

branches.en: Meaning and style twisted out of shape.
branches.cn: 被扭曲的意义与文风。

branches.en: The rope image carried into roads and mechanics.
branches.cn: 绳索意象被带入道路与力学。

intro.en: The word comes from a Latin twisting stem with -ura, and English adds -ed, -er, -ous, and the parallel -uous.
intro.cn: 本词由拉丁语「扭绞」词干加 -ura 构成，英语再加 -ed、-er、-ous 以及平行的 -uous。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the twisting verb, its noun, and the related noun for torment.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁词条给出「扭绞」动词、其名词以及相关的「苦痛」名词。

items.example: The stem is the twisted body of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干是这个词被扭过的主体。

items.example: Tortura is the act of twisting.
Tortured means having been tortured.
Torturer names the one who acts.
Torturous means full of torture.
Tortuous means full of twists.
Torque keeps the physical sense.
Tort is the legal cousin of the word.
items.exampleCN: tort 是本词的法律亲属。

items.example: Torment is the sister noun of suffering.
items.exampleCN: torment 是表示苦痛的姊妹名词。

definition_zh: 总的；总计的；完全的；全部；总数；合计达
definition_en: the whole amount of something, or complete and entire, or to add up to a figure
core_image: 一长串账单被最后一道横线压住，末尾写着一个整整齐齐的数
scene: 结账时收银条一路打印到纸尾，最下面那一行加粗。The total for the trip came to more than we had planned.
sceneCN: 这里 total 是「总数、总额」（第 4 个义项：所有部分相加之和）；句意为这趟旅行的总额超出了我们的计划。画面里有长条小票、最末那行加粗的数字。

pos.zh: 形容词：总的；全部的；完全的

derivatives.zh: 加 -ly 构成，义为「完全地；全部地」
加 -ity 构成，义为「整体；全部」
加前缀 sub- 构成，义为「小计；部分合计」
由 total 派生的政治术语，义为「极权的」

senses.title: The whole amount
senses.definition: the complete amount obtained by adding all the parts together
senses.definitionCN: 把所有部分相加所得的完整数量
senses.example: The total of the two bills was surprisingly small.
senses.exampleCN: 两张账单的总额小得令人意外。
senses.why: The Latin word for the whole is the direct source, so the noun names the sum in its completeness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中表示「整体」的词是直接来源，故名词指完整加总后的量。

senses.title: Adding up to a figure
senses.definition: to amount to a particular figure when all parts are counted
senses.definitionCN: 各部分组成加总起来达到某个数字
senses.example: The costs totalled more than three thousand yuan.
senses.exampleCN: 这些花费合计超过三千元。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb: to make a total out of scattered items.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：把零散的项加总成一个总数。

senses.title: Complete and absolute
senses.definition: used of something with no part missing or no exception allowed
senses.definitionCN: 用于毫无缺失或毫无例外的情形
senses.example: The room fell into total silence when she began to speak.
senses.exampleCN: 她开口时，屋子里一片死寂。
senses.why: If a total is everything, then a total silence is silence without one sound left out.
senses.whyCN: 既然总数意味着全部，那么 total silence 就是一点声音也没遗漏的静。

senses.title: A sum of money owed
senses.definition: the full sum due for goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 为货物或服务应付的全部款项
senses.example: Please pay the total within seven days of the invoice.
senses.exampleCN: 请在开票后七天内付清总额。
senses.why: Shops print the total at the bottom of a receipt, since it is the last and whole figure.
senses.whyCN: 商店把小票底部的那个数叫作 total，因为它是最后也是完整的那个数。

senses.title: Counting everything in
senses.definition: including every member or part, as in the total number of students
senses.definitionCN: 包括每个成员或每个部分，如学生总人数
senses.example: The total number of students rose by two hundred this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年学生总人数增加了两百。
senses.why: The adjective marks a count that leaves nothing outside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记一种不把任何东西留在外面的计数。

senses.title: A whole in philosophy
senses.definition: in older philosophical writing, the whole made of parts that hang together
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的哲学文字中，指由相联部分构成的整体
senses.example: The old textbook speaks of the total as more than the sum of its parts.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧教材说整体大于其各部分之和。
senses.why: Philosophy uses the word for any whole that holds together, which is the root idea unextended.
senses.whyCN: 哲学用这个词指任何自成一体的整体，这正是未加引申的词根本义。

senses.title: Complete ruin in expressions
senses.definition: used in phrases such as a total loss to mean damage beyond recovery
senses.definitionCN: 用于 a total loss 等短语，表示彻底损失、无法挽回
senses.example: The storm left the boat a total loss.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴使那条船彻底报废。
senses.why: Insurance language needs a word for damage with nothing left to save, and total supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 保险用语需要一个词表示无可挽回的损毁，total 正好提供。

senses.title: Everything considered
senses.definition: used in phrases like in total or a total of to introduce a final count
senses.definitionCN: 用于 in total 或 a total of 等短语引出最终计数
senses.example: A total of forty people signed the sheet.
senses.exampleCN: 共有四十人在表上签了字。
senses.why: The phrase works like a bracket around a list, closing it with one figure.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语像一对括号把一串项目包起来，再用一个数字收尾。

intro.en: Total comes from medieval Latin totalis, an adjective from totus, the Latin word for whole or entire, and it entered English through French.
intro.cn: total 来自中世纪拉丁语 totalis，是 totus（意为「整个、全部」）的形容词，经由法语进入英语。

items.en: Totus means all, whole, or entire, and it has no parts to be counted separately.
items.cn: 拉丁语 totus 意为「全部、整个」，它本身不再被拆成可数的部分。

items.en: The derived adjective totalis names what belongs to the whole rather than to a part.
items.cn: 由它派生的形容词 totalis 指属于整体而非属于部分的。

items.en: Old French takes total as an adjective of the schools and of accounts.
items.cn: 古法语把 total 用作学校与账目中的形容词。

items.en: Middle English borrows the adjective and soon uses it as a noun for the sum.
items.cn: 中古英语借入这个形容词，很快又把它用作表示总和的名称。

items.en: The verb to total appears in the eighteenth century in bookkeeping and in arithmetic.
items.cn: 动词 total 于十八世纪出现在簿记与算术中。

items.en: The emphatic sense of complete, as in total silence, spreads in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 表示「完全」的强调义（如 total silence）在十九、二十世纪扩散开来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms on the same stem, while the near-meaning group gathers words for sums and for completeness.
note.cn: 形近组收集同一词干的形式，近义组则汇集表示总和与完整性的词。

normalIntro.en: These memories use the fixed phrases in total and a total of, the bookkeeping verb, and the emphatic use with abstract nouns.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用 in total 与 a total of 的固定搭配、簿记中的动词用法，以及与抽象名词连用时的强调用法。

normal.en: In total and a total of both close a list with one figure.
normal.cn: in total 与 a total of 都用同一个数字为一串项目收尾。

normal.en: A total loss is insurance language, and it means nothing can be saved.
normal.cn: a total loss 是保险用语，意思是无可挽救。

normal.en: The verb is written totalled in British spelling and totaled in American spelling.
normal.cn: 动词在英式拼写中写作 totalled，美式写作 totaled。

normal.en: Total silence means no sound at all, which shows how the word moves from sums to absolutes.
normal.cn: total silence 指一点声音也没有，这显示该词如何从加总走向绝对。

normal.en: Subtotal takes the prefix sub- and gives the sum below the main one.
normal.cn: subtotal 加前缀 sub-，给出主总额之下的那个小计。

abstract.en: Picture a column of figures and a single line ruled under the last of them.
abstract.cn: 想象一列数字，最后一行下面划着一道横线。

abstract.en: Think of an empty room where even the echo has stopped.
abstract.cn: 想一间空房，连回声都停了。

abstract.en: A total leaves nothing outside it, whether it counts money or measures silence.
abstract.cn: 总数不把任何东西留在外面，无论它数的是钱，还是衡量的是静。

examples.en: In total, the project took eleven months to finish.
examples.cn: 这个项目总共用了十一个月才完成。

examples.en: He was in total agreement with the plan.
examples.cn: 他完全同意这个计划。

examples.en: The company's sales totalled nearly two million units last year.
examples.cn: 去年公司的销量合计接近两百万台。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「头托」——把所有数一起托到头上，就是总数 total。

root: 拉丁语 totus（全部、整个）→ 中世纪拉丁语 totalis → 古法语 total → 英语 total。同族词有 totality、subtotal；totus 还与 totidem（同样多）同源。

sensesIntro.en: The entry begins with the added-up sum, then follows the same whole into the verbs of counting, the adjective of completeness, and the emphatic phrases of absolute loss or silence.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从加总求和开始，再沿「整体」这一概念走入计数的动词、表示完整的形容词，以及「彻底损失」「彻底寂静」这类强调短语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole closed by a ruled line.
core.cn: 核心意象：被一道横线封住的整体。

branches.en: The sum itself and the phrases that present it.
branches.cn: 总和本身以及呈现它的短语。

branches.en: The act of adding parts into a figure.
branches.cn: 把各部分加成一个数字的动作。

branches.en: Completeness and the total count.
branches.cn: 完整性与全部计数。

branches.en: The philosophical whole.
branches.cn: 哲学意义上的整体。

branches.en: Total loss as damage with nothing left.
branches.cn: 彻底损失指无可挽回的损毁。

items.example: Totality is the state of being whole.
A subtotal is a sum below the main one.

Totalling the column took a minute.

items.example: Totals serves both uses.

definition_zh: 完全地；彻底地；绝对地（口语）
definition_en: completely, in every part, or used in speech to mean absolutely or very much
core_image: 一杯水被倒得齐到杯沿，一滴也不差，没有任何余地
scene: 朋友改了三次时间，最后发来一句：I totally forgot about the meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 totally 是口语中的强调副词「完全、彻底」（第 1 个义项：完全地）；句意为「我完全忘了开会这件事」。画面里有手机屏幕上的那条消息与已经改过三次的时间。

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词词尾 -ly，义为「总的；完全的」
同族名词，义为「整体；全部」
近义副词，义为「完全地」，语义几乎重合
由 part 加 -ly 构成的反义副词，义为「部分地」

senses.title: In every part
senses.definition: in a complete way, with no part left out
senses.definitionCN: 以完整的方式，没有任何部分被遗漏
senses.example: The two designs are totally different in spirit.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个设计在精神上完全不同。
senses.why: The adverb simply adds -ly to total, so it says the whole of something is affected.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词只是给 total 加上 -ly，所以它表示某物的全部受到影响。

senses.title: Used for emphasis in speech
senses.definition: in informal speech, used to strengthen a statement or a feeling
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用来加强陈述或感受
senses.example: I totally forgot that we had moved the class.
senses.exampleCN: 我完全忘了我们把课换了时间。
senses.why: Speakers reach for an absolute word when a plain very feels too weak, and totally supplies that force.
senses.whyCN: 当单说 very 显得力量不够时，说话人就找一个绝对的词，totally 正好提供这种力度。

senses.title: With no reservation
senses.definition: used with verbs of agreement or support to show no doubt or condition
senses.definitionCN: 与同意、支持类动词连用，表示没有疑问或条件
senses.example: She totally agrees with the new timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 她完全同意新的时间表。
senses.why: Agreeing totally leaves no part of the matter open, which is the literal sense applied to opinion.
senses.whyCN: 完全同意意味着这件事没有留下任何疑问，正是字面义用在意见上。

senses.title: To the last degree
senses.definition: used before adjectives to mean to the highest degree, often for something negative
senses.definitionCN: 置于形容词前表示程度最高，常用于负面事物
senses.example: The whole arrangement was totally unacceptable to the staff.
senses.exampleCN: 整个安排对员工来说完全不可接受。
senses.why: The word works like a scale pushed to its end, which is why it pairs so often with extreme adjectives.
senses.whyCN: 这个词像一把推到尽头的刻度，所以它常与表示极端的形容词搭配。

senses.title: Not partly but wholly
senses.definition: used to contrast a complete state with a partial one
senses.definitionCN: 用来对比完整状态与部分状态
senses.example: The room was not partly dark; it was totally dark.
senses.exampleCN: 房间不是有些暗，而是完全漆黑。
senses.why: The contrast sense shows the word at its clearest, since partly and totally are the two ends of one scale.
senses.whyCN: 对比用法最能显出这个词的含义，因为 partly 与 totally 是同一天平的两端。

senses.title: Complete in a judgement
senses.definition: used in judgements such as totally right or totally fair
senses.definitionCN: 用于 totally right、totally fair 等评价中
senses.example: His answer was totally right, though nobody expected it.
senses.exampleCN: 他的答案完全正确，尽管没人料到。
senses.why: A judgement that admits no exception takes the same adverb as a physical whole.
senses.whyCN: 不承认任何例外的评价，用的副词与物理上的「整体」相同。

senses.title: Entirely dependent
senses.definition: used with verbs of depending or relying to mean with nothing else to fall back on
senses.definitionCN: 与依赖类动词连用，表示别无依靠
senses.example: The village is totally dependent on the single well.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子完全依赖那口唯一的井。
senses.why: Here the completeness is about need: no other source exists to share the load.
senses.whyCN: 这里的完整性说的是需要：再没有别的来源分担。

senses.title: In modern casual use
senses.definition: in very casual speech, a filler-like intensifier in statements of feeling
senses.definitionCN: 在极随意的口语中，作为带填充色彩的强调词出现在表达感受的句子里
senses.example: It was totally the best trip we have ever taken.
senses.exampleCN: 这真的是我们玩得最好的一趟旅行。
senses.why: Intensifiers drift toward filler in relaxed speech, and totally has become one of the commonest.
senses.whyCN: 强调词在轻松口语里会向虚词漂移，totally 已成了最常见的之一。

intro.en: Totally is the adverb of total, made by adding the English suffix -ly to the adjective borrowed from French and Latin, and its emphatic conversational use is very recent.
intro.cn: totally 是 total 的副词，由借自法语与拉丁语的形容词加上英语后缀 -ly 构成；它带强调意味的口语用法则出现得很晚。

items.en: Totus means whole, and totalis describes what belongs to the whole.
items.cn: 拉丁语 totus 意为「整个」，totalis 描述属于整体的东西。

items.en: Old French hands the adjective total to Middle English with accounts and schooling.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词 total 连同账目与学校的语境一起交给中古英语。

items.en: The adverb is formed in English with -ly, as happened to most adjectives of French origin.
items.cn: 这个副词在英语中用 -ly 构成，正如大多数源自法语的形容词一样。

items.en: In the nineteenth century totally is a somewhat formal word of written prose.
items.cn: 在十九世纪，totally 还是一个偏正式的书面词。

items.en: The twentieth century brings the word into everyday speech as an intensifier.
items.cn: 二十世纪这个词进入日常口语，成为强调词。

items.en: In the last decades totally spreads as a casual filler in youth speech.
items.cn: 近几十年来 totally 作为随意的填充强调词在年轻人的言语中扩散。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on total, while the near-meaning group gathers the adverbs and adjectives of completeness.
note.cn: 形近组收集由 total 构成的形式，近义组则汇集表示完整性的副词与形容词。

normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用这个词的常见搭配、它与 partly 的对照，以及它在现代口语中的位置。

normal.en: Totally agrees and totally different are the two everyday collocations.
normal.cn: totally agree 与 totally different 是两个天天用的搭配。

normal.en: The word is written with two l's in the middle and ends in -ly.
normal.cn: 这个词中间有两个 l，末尾是 -ly。

normal.en: Partly and totally are two ends of the same scale.
normal.cn: partly 与 totally 是同一天平的两端。

normal.en: In young speech, totally often carries no more weight than really.
normal.cn: 在年轻人的言语中，totally 常常和 really 差不多重。

normal.en: The base form is total, and the adverb simply adds -ly.
normal.cn: 基础形式是 total，副词只是加 -ly。

abstract.en: Picture a glass filled exactly to the rim, not a drop more possible.
abstract.cn: 想象一只杯子正好倒到杯沿，再多一滴都不可能。

abstract.en: Think of two roads that never come close after leaving the square.
abstract.cn: 想两条路从广场分开后再也不靠近。

abstract.en: The word pushes a scale all the way to the end and leaves no room for a maybe.
abstract.cn: 这个词把刻度一直推到尽头，不给「也许」留空位。

examples.en: Her reaction was totally different from what I had expected.
examples.cn: 她的反应和我想的完全不同。

examples.en: I totally agree with what the report says about safety.
examples.cn: 我完全同意报告里关于安全的说法。

examples.en: The old town is totally dependent on visitors in summer.
examples.cn: 这座老城在夏天完全依赖游客。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「头特利」——一刀切到头，干脆利落，就是完全地 totally。

root: total（拉丁语 totus「全部」）＋副词后缀 -ly。同族词有 total、totality、subtotal；totus 亦为 totidem「同样多」的词根。

sensesIntro.en: The entry starts from the plain idea of complete coverage, then shows the same force in speech emphasis, in judgement, in dependence, and finally in the casual filler use of modern speech.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从「覆盖全部」的朴素意思开始，再把这份力量依次放到口语强调、评价、依赖上，最后是现代口语里的填充强调用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a measure pushed to its end.
core.cn: 核心意象：刻度被推到尽头。

branches.en: Full coverage, in contrast with partly.
branches.cn: 完全覆盖，与 partly 相对。

branches.en: Emphasis and casual filler in speech.
branches.cn: 口语中的强调与填充用法。

branches.en: Agreement and judgement without exception.
branches.cn: 毫无例外的同意与评价。

branches.en: Degree pushed to the extreme.
branches.cn: 推到极端的程度。

branches.en: Need with no other source.
branches.cn: 别无所依的需要。

intro.en: The adverb is one root plus one suffix, and its wider family comes from -ity and the prefix sub-.
intro.cn: 这个副词是一个词根加一个后缀，更大的词族来自 -ity 与前缀 sub-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give totus and the words formed beside it.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁词条给出 totus 及其旁生的词。

items.example: Total is the base of the adverb.
Totus is the ultimate root.
Totalis gives total.
Total plus -ly gives totally.
Totality means wholeness.
A subtotal is below the total.
Partly is the opposite pole.
Partly is built on part.
items.exampleCN: partly 由 part 加 -ly 构成。

items.example: A total loss is a settled insurance term.
items.exampleCN: a total loss 是固定的保险术语。

definition_zh: 触摸；接触；触觉；少量；联系；感动；涉及
definition_en: to put a hand or an object lightly against something, or the act and sense of such contact
core_image: 指尖轻轻碰到冰凉的玻璃，只留下一圈几乎看不见的雾
scene: 展厅里隔着护栏，讲解员举起手示意不许靠近。Please do not touch the paintings on the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 touch 是动词「触摸、碰」（第 1 个义项：用手或物体轻触某物）；句意为请不要触摸墙上的画。画面里有护栏、伸出的手与墙上的画框。

pos.zh: 动词：触摸；碰到；感动；涉及
名词：触摸；触觉；少量；联系

derivatives.zh: 加 -ing 构成，义为「动人的；感人的」
加 -ed 构成，义为「感动的；有点疯的（口语）」
加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「未触动过的；未受影响的」
拉丁同源形容词，义为「触觉的」

senses.title: To put a hand on something
senses.definition: to put a hand or finger on something, especially lightly
senses.definitionCN: 用手或手指轻放在某物上，尤指轻轻地
senses.example: She touched the cold glass to feel where the crack began.
senses.exampleCN: 她摸着冰凉的玻璃，想找出裂纹从何处开始。
senses.why: The French verb tocher gave English a word for the light contact of one thing on another.
senses.whyCN: 古法语动词 tocher 为英语提供了表示一物与另一物轻触的词。

senses.title: An act of contact
senses.definition: the state or act of two things being in contact
senses.definitionCN: 两物相互接触的状态或动作
senses.example: A single touch of the wire set off the alarm.
senses.exampleCN: 电线被碰了一下，警报就响了。
senses.why: The verb and the noun are the same idea seen from two sides, one as action and one as event.
senses.whyCN: 动词与名词是同一概念的两面，一为动作，一为事件。

senses.title: The sense of feeling
senses.definition: the ability of the skin to feel what comes against it
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤感知接触物的能力
senses.example: After the accident he lost the touch in two fingers.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后他两根手指失去了触觉。
senses.why: Among the five senses, touch is the one that works only by direct contact, which is why the word names it.
senses.whyCN: 五官之中，触觉是唯一靠直接接触起作用的，这个词正因此用来命名它。

senses.title: A small amount
senses.definition: a very small quantity of something, often added to a dish or a colour
senses.definitionCN: 极少的一点，常指添进菜肴或颜色的部分
senses.example: Add a touch of salt to the soup before serving.
senses.exampleCN: 上桌前在汤里加一点盐。
senses.why: A small amount is like a fingertip of something, just enough to be felt but not taken in bulk.
senses.whyCN: 少量就像指尖沾到的那一点，感觉得到，却谈不上分量。

senses.title: Contact between people
senses.definition: the state of communicating with someone, as in keep in touch
senses.definitionCN: 与人保持交流的状态，如 keep in touch
senses.example: We stayed in touch after we left the same school.
senses.exampleCN: 离开同一所学校后我们一直保持联系。
senses.why: People who correspond are in contact even at a distance, so the physical word carries over to communication.
senses.whyCN: 保持来往的人即便相隔也处于「接触」中，于是物理的词被挪用到交流上。

senses.title: To move someone deeply
senses.definition: to cause a strong feeling of sympathy or gratitude
senses.definitionCN: 引起强烈的同情或感激之情
senses.example: The letter from her old teacher touched her more than any gift.
senses.exampleCN: 老教师的那封信比任何礼物都让她感动。
senses.why: A feeling is said to reach the heart as a hand reaches the skin, so being moved is being touched.
senses.whyCN: 情感像手触到皮肤那样抵达心里，所以被感动就是被 touch 到。

senses.title: To deal with a subject
senses.definition: to mention or deal with a matter briefly
senses.definitionCN: 简短地提到或处理某个问题
senses.example: The report touches on housing but says little about cost.
senses.exampleCN: 报告谈及住房，却很少提到成本。
senses.why: To touch a subject is to come into contact with it lightly, without taking it up fully.
senses.whyCN: touch 一个话题就是轻轻碰到它，并不把它完全展开。

senses.title: A slight trace of a quality
senses.definition: a slight trace of a quality, as in a touch of sadness
senses.definitionCN: 某种特质的一丝痕迹，如 a touch of sadness
senses.example: There was a touch of frost on the windows this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 今早窗上有一层薄霜。
senses.why: The sense of a small quantity extends from food to weather and to mood, wherever a trace can be noticed.
senses.whyCN: 「少量」义从食物扩展到天气与心情，凡是能察觉出痕迹的地方都能用。

senses.title: Skill with the hands
senses.definition: a special skill in handling something, as in the common touch or a fine touch
senses.definitionCN: 处理某物时的特别本领，如 the common touch 或 a fine touch
senses.example: The old cook still had a fine touch with pastry.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老厨子做起酥点来仍然手法精到。
senses.why: Skill shows in how the hand meets the material, so a good worker is said to have a good touch.
senses.whyCN: 手艺体现在手与材料相接的方式上，所以好手艺被说成有好的 touch。

senses.title: In football and rugby
senses.definition: in rugby and some other games, the area at the side of the field, or the act of grounding the ball
senses.definitionCN: 在橄榄球等运动中指场边区域，或把球触地的动作
senses.example: The ball went into touch and the line-out followed.
senses.exampleCN: 球出了边线，随后进行边线掷球。
senses.why: The sporting use keeps the literal sense: the ball leaves the field by touching the boundary.
senses.whyCN: 体育用法保留了字面义：球碰到边线而离开场地。

intro.en: Touch comes from Old French tochier, from a Vulgar Latin verb built on a root meaning to knock or strike, and it has been used for both contact and feeling since the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: touch 来自古法语 tochier，其源是表示「敲、击」词根的通俗拉丁语动词；自中世纪以来既指接触，也指感受。

items.en: A Vulgar Latin verb related to toccare means to knock or strike lightly against something.
items.cn: 与 toccare 相关的通俗拉丁语动词意为轻敲或轻击某物。

items.en: Old French tochier carries the senses of touching, tasting, and trying.
items.cn: 古法语 tochier 兼有触摸、品尝与尝试诸义。

items.en: Middle English touchen appears in the thirteenth century for physical contact.
items.cn: 中古英语 touchen 在十三世纪出现，表示身体上的接触。

items.en: The sense of moving the feelings is recorded early, since the heart was thought to be struck by emotion.
items.cn: 「感动」义很早就有了，因为当时认为情感会击中心。

items.en: The phrase keep in touch grows out of the older idea of hands meeting in greeting.
items.cn: keep in touch 这一说法源自更早的「以手相握致意」的想法。

items.en: Touch screens and touch typing make the word name any contact used to give a command.
items.cn: 触摸屏与盲打让这个词指任何用来下达指令的接触。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derivative and compound forms, while the near-meaning group gathers verbs for contact and for feeling.
note.cn: 形近组收集派生与复合形式，近义组则汇集表示接触与感受的动词。

entries.definition: moving the feelings
affected with gratitude or sympathy
not touched or not affected
entries.definitionCN: 未被触碰的；未受影响的

entries.definition: a burning light carried in the hand
entries.definitionCN: 火把；手电，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to sense by touching or in the mind
the state of touching or communicating
to move a hand gently along something
to cause a strong feeling in someone

normalIntro.en: These memories use the fixed phrase in touch, the quantity sense with of, and the way a physical verb grows into a word for feeling.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用 in touch 的固定说法、a touch of 的数量用法，以及一个物理动词长成情感词的路径。

normal.en: Keep in touch is about writing and calling, not about hands.
normal.cn: keep in touch 说的是写信打电话，与手无关。

normal.en: A touch of salt and a touch of frost both mean a very small amount.
normal.cn: a touch of salt 与 a touch of frost 都指极少的一点。

normal.en: Touch on a subject means to mention it lightly, never to treat it fully.
normal.cn: touch on a subject 指轻轻提到，从不彻底处理。

normal.en: In rugby, the ball goes into touch when it crosses the side line.
normal.cn: 在橄榄球中，球越过边线就叫出 touch。

normal.en: The adjective touching keeps the feeling sense: a touching story moves you.
normal.cn: 形容词 touching 保留感受义：a touching story 让你感动。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip on cold glass and the faint print it leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象指尖按在冰凉的玻璃上，留下淡淡的印。

abstract.en: Think of two wires just meeting, and the whole machine starting up.
abstract.cn: 想两根线刚刚接上，整台机器就启动了。

abstract.en: One light contact is enough to carry either information or feeling.
abstract.cn: 轻轻一次接触，就足以传递信息，也足以传递情感。

examples.en: Do not touch the wet paint on the bench.
examples.cn: 别碰长椅上还没干的油漆。

examples.en: We lost touch for years and then met again at a wedding.
examples.cn: 我们失联多年，后来在一场婚礼上重逢。

examples.en: Her speech touched everyone in the hall.
examples.cn: 她的演讲感动了礼堂里的每一个人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踏实」——手指一碰到就踏实了，能碰到才算真。

root: 通俗拉丁语 toccare（轻敲）→ 古法语 tochier → 中古英语 touchen → 现代 touch。同族词有 touching、untouched；拉丁词根亦见 tactile「触觉的」。

sensesIntro.en: The entry starts from the light contact of the hand, then takes in the sense of feeling, a small amount, human contact, being moved, and finally the technical uses in talk and in sport.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从手的轻触写起，再收进触觉、少量、人际往来、感动，最后是谈话与体育中的专门用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fingertip meeting a surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：指尖与表面相接。

branches.en: Contact, the act of contact, and the sense that reads it.
branches.cn: 接触、接触的动作与读取它的触觉。

branches.en: A small quantity and a trace of a quality.
branches.cn: 少量与某种特质的一丝痕迹。

branches.en: Keeping in touch and touching on a subject.
branches.cn: 保持联系与谈及某个话题。

branches.en: Being moved by feeling.
branches.cn: 被情感所动。

branches.en: Skill of hand, and the touch line in sport.
branches.cn: 手上的技巧与体育中的边线。

intro.en: The word is a borrowed verb that also works as a noun; its family grows with -ing, -ed, un-, and compounds with screen and down.
intro.cn: 本词是兼作名词的借入动词，其词族靠 -ing、-ed、un- 以及与 screen、down 等合成扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the root of knocking and its tactile relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁词条给出「敲击」词根及其触觉相关的同族词。

items.example: The stem comes from Old French.
Toccare underlies the Romance forms.
items.exampleCN: toccare 是罗曼语诸形式的基础。

items.example: Tochier is the direct source.
Touching means moving.
Touched means affected.
Untouched means not touched.
Touchable surfaces can be handled.
A touch screen needs a finger.
A touch down is worth five points.

definition_zh: 坚韧的；难对付的；艰难的；强硬的；粗暴的；硬汉
definition_en: strong and not easily broken, torn, or defeated; also difficult to deal with or to bear
core_image: 一块旧皮带被反复拉扯，纹路皱起却始终不断
scene: 面试失败第三次，他回家的路上忽然笑了一下。That was a tough year, but it taught me a lot.
sceneCN: 这里 tough 是「艰难的、难熬的」（第 3 个义项：难以应付或难以忍受）；句意为那是艰难的一年，但让我学到了很多。画面里有雨后的街道、走回家的人影。

pos.zh: 形容词：坚韧的；艰难的；强硬的；粗暴的
动词（口语）：坚持；挺过（常与 out 连用）

derivatives.zh: 加 -ness 构成，义为「坚韧；强硬」
加 -ly 构成，义为「强硬地；艰难地」
加动词后缀 -en 构成，义为「使变坚韧；使变强硬」
加 -ie 构成，口语义为「难题；难对付的人」

senses.title: Strong and hard to break
senses.definition: strong enough to bend or wear without breaking
senses.definitionCN: 强度足以弯曲磨损而不断裂
senses.example: The old fishing line was still tough after twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这根旧钓线过了二十年依然结实。
senses.why: The Old English word describes what can bear force without giving way, and that physical strength is the base of every other sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词描述能受力而不屈服之物，这份物理上的强韧是其他一切含义的基础。

senses.title: Hard to chew
senses.definition: of food, difficult to cut or chew
senses.definitionCN: 指食物难切难嚼
senses.example: The meat was tough and took an hour to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 这肉很老，吃了一个小时才吃完。
senses.why: If a material resists force, then a piece of meat that resists the teeth is tough in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 材料若抗得住外力，那块抗得住牙齿的肉也就同样被称作 tough。

senses.title: Difficult to bear
senses.definition: hard to endure or to live through
senses.definitionCN: 难以忍受或难以度过
senses.example: It was a tough winter with no work and little money.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个没有工作又缺钱的难熬冬天。
senses.why: A hard period strains a person the way force strains a material, so the physical word takes on the sense of hardship.
senses.whyCN: 艰难的日子像外力拉扯材料那样拉扯着人，于是物理词带上了艰苦之义。

senses.title: Requiring effort
senses.definition: needing much effort or skill to deal with
senses.definitionCN: 需要很多努力或技巧才能处理
senses.example: The last question was the toughest one on the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一道题是卷子上最难的一道。
senses.why: A task that resists solution is like a material that resists force, and tough comes to mean difficult.
senses.whyCN: 难解的任务如抗力的材料，于是 tough 被用来表示困难。

senses.title: Severe and firm
senses.definition: firm and severe in dealing with people or crime
senses.definitionCN: 对待人或犯罪时坚定而严厉
senses.example: The city took a tough line on illegal parking.
senses.exampleCN: 该市对违章停车采取了强硬立场。
senses.why: A firm policy does not bend under pressure, which is the physical sense applied to rules.
senses.whyCN: 坚定的政策在压力下不弯，正是物理义用在规则上。

senses.title: Rough in manner
senses.definition: violent or rough in behaviour, often of a neighbourhood or a group
senses.definitionCN: 行为凶悍粗野，常用于街区或人群
senses.example: He grew up in a tough part of town and learned to walk fast.
senses.exampleCN: 他在城里凶悍的街区长大，学会了走路快。
senses.why: A place where one must be strong to survive is called tough, transferring the quality of the person to the place.
senses.whyCN: 一个必须强硬才能活下来的地方也被称作 tough，人的品质被移到了地方上。

senses.title: A rough person
senses.definition: in informal use, a violent person or, admiringly, a strong one
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指凶暴的人，或带钦佩地指硬汉
senses.example: A few toughs were hanging around the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 几个混混在街角晃荡。
senses.why: The adjective is used as a noun, so a person with the quality comes to be named by it.
senses.whyCN: 形容词被当作名词用，于是具有这种品质的人就被它命名。

senses.title: To endure to the end
senses.definition: in informal use, to keep going through something hard, especially with out
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示在难事里坚持到底，尤与 out 连用
senses.example: The team had to tough it out until the storm passed.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍只得硬撑着等风暴过去。
senses.why: The verb turns strength into action: to stay firm until the difficulty is over.
senses.whyCN: 动词把强韧变成动作：一直挺住直到难事过去。

intro.en: Tough is an Old English adjective of strength, related to the verb for pulling, and its many figurative senses all rest on the idea of something that does not give way.
intro.cn: tough 是古英语中表示强韧的形容词，与「拉」的动词同源，其众多引申义都建立在「不肯屈服」这一想法上。

items.en: Toh describes what is strong and firm, and it is used of wood, leather, and rope.
items.cn: 古英语 toh 描述坚固结实之物，用于木、皮与绳索。

items.en: The stem is related to Old Norse tog, a rope or a pull, so strength and pulling belong together.
items.cn: 这个词干与古诺斯语 tog（绳、拉扯）相关，强韧与拉扯本是一体。

items.en: Middle English extends the word to food that resists the teeth and to people who resist hardship.
items.cn: 中古英语把该词扩展到抗齿的食物，也用于抗得住苦难的人。

items.en: The sense of a difficult task or a hard time appears and becomes the dominant everyday use.
items.cn: 「难办的事、艰难时期」义出现，并成为日常最主要的用法。

items.en: American English develops the admiring use of tough for a strong, unshakable person.
items.cn: 美式英语发展出带钦佩意味的 tough，指坚强不可动摇的人。

items.en: The casual verb to tough it out spreads in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 口语动词 tough it out 在二十世纪流行开来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms with the same spelling pattern, while the near-meaning group gathers words for strength and for difficulty.
note.cn: 形近组收集拼写相近的形式，近义组则汇集表示强韧与困难的词。

to make stronger or firmer
a difficult problem or person
despite the fact that
